Pretrial disclosures (trap): Thirty days before the final pretrial conference: serve a final witness list (supplement within 5 days, then only with leave), exchange exhibit lists and deposition designations, make exhibits available for inspection, and serve a damages list. Counter-designations are due within 7 days. Written objections to authenticity or admissibility must be filed at least 14 days before the final pretrial conference, or they are waived absent good cause. Noncompliance can exclude the items from your case-in-chief.

docs.x: Judge Jill E. McCook, E.D. Tenn.. Final pretrial order (trap): Plaintiff serves a draft 45 days before the final pretrial conference; defendant supplies its theory and objections within 5 business days. If the parties cannot agree, plaintiff must notify chambers at least 21 days before the conference. Missing this or failing to file an agreed order may be treated as failure to prosecute and lead to dismissal under Rule 41(b). The proposed order is filed 5 days before the conference. It must include numbered stipulated facts (agree on everything without a reasonable basis for dispute), each claim and defense in a separately numbered paragraph with its legal theory and supporting facts (vague or conclusory statements are unacceptable), contested and novel legal issues, the method for calculating disputed damages, and trial length in 8-hour days. docs.t: Judge Jill E. McCook (E.D. Tenn.) — Filings before trial
docs.x: Judge Jill E. McCook, E.D. Tenn.. Filings before trial: At least 7 days before trial: file a final witness list limited to witnesses who will actually testify, a damages list (stipulated preferred), deposition designations and counter-designations, expert resumes, and briefs on contested legal issues, and jointly submit pre-marked exhibits numbered sequentially (plaintiff’s first, defendant’s continuing from plaintiff’s last number). Jury cases: file a single set of proposed stipulated jury instructions at least 10 days before trial. A disputed instruction goes under one heading with each side’s version and a one-paragraph statement with authority, and all instructions appear in sequence in one document; cite any model source. docs.t: Judge Jill E. McCook (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Jill E. McCook, E.D. Tenn.. Trial: Trial starts at 9:00 a.m. in Courtroom 3A, Knoxville; if there are preliminary matters, notify chambers and be present at 8:30 a.m. Tell the courtroom deputy at least 2 days ahead if you will use the evidence presentation system. Exhibits must be submitted in electronic format for JERS; providing them to the courtroom deputy (preferably on USB, DVD, or CD) at least 7 days before trial is strongly encouraged. Move exhibits in individually, not collectively. Videotaped testimony must be pre-marked and made available to the other side. Question witnesses from the podium; only one lawyer per side may address a given witness. The court conducts general voir dire and counsel may supplement. Examination beyond redirect and recross is discouraged; no written Rule 50 motion is required. Jurors may take notes and take exhibits to the jury room. During delib

docs.t: Judge Jill E. McCook (E.D. Tenn.) — Mediation
docs.x: Judge Jill E. McCook, E.D. Tenn.. Mediation: Mediation is allowed and encouraged, and reasonable extensions of deadlines and trial dates to pursue it are granted. The form orders also require a joint report 22 weeks before trial on whether and when the case should be mediated (or why not).

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Summary judgment (trap): Judge Crytzer will not consider any fact or argument not raised in the motion and supporting memorandum (with exhibits) or the response (with exhibits). That includes any separate “Statement of Undisputed Material Facts” or response to one, which may be struck, with any brief relying on it to be refiled (citing L.R. 7.1(a), (b), and (d) and the 25-page limit). Cross-motions for summary judgment should generally be briefed independently. Responses to dispositive motions are due in 21 days (L.R. 7.1(a)).

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Communications and extensions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Communications and extensions (trap): Letters and emails (Crytzer_Chambers@tned.uscourts.gov) only for routine matters such as scheduling or settlement, and emergencies, never the merits; copy all counsel, and include all parties on calls where possible. Law clerks give no legal advice. To reset a hearing or extend a deadline, file a motion on the record; the court will not act on email requests absent emergency. A Rule 6(b) extension motion should state the standard with specific supporting facts, ask for a date certain or a set number of days, and say whether it is unopposed. The scheduling order changes only for good cause in strict compliance with Rule 6(b).

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Hearings and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Hearings and courtesy copies: All hearings are in person unless the court says otherwise or a party asks; Rule 16 and case management conferences may be by phone case by case. Final pretrial conferences, civil and criminal, are in person in Knoxville. Motions are usually decided without a hearing (L.R. 7.2), but a party may request one. If presenting evidence at a scheduled hearing, notify chambers in advance. No regular courtesy copies. If you must file at the last minute before a hearing or trial, promptly deliver a hard copy to chambers and bring one to court. For emergency motions, also email the motion and supporting papers to chambers, copying all counsel.

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Page limits and sealing
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Page limits and sealing: Requests to exceed Local Rule 7.1(b) page limits are denied unless good cause is shown; noncompliant portions may be disregarded or the motion summarily denied. Also comply with Local Rule 5.1. Confidentiality designations do not justify sealing; move for leave under Rule 26(c) and Local Rule 26.2, consider whether only portions need sealing, and expect close scrutiny.

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery (trap): Discovery generally runs about 6 months in a standard case and closes about 5.5 months before trial; serve written requests early enough that responses fall due before the deadline. Duplicative or overly burdensome discovery is not permitted. Before any motion to compel, meet and confer, then call the assigned magistrate judge’s chambers for a telephone conference. Only if the dispute survives that conference may you file a motion, which must certify compliance (plus the Rule 37(a)(1) certification if applicable).

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Experts and Daubert (trap)
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Experts and Daubert (trap): Sample order: plaintiff’s experts about 8 months before trial, defendant’s about 7 months, rebuttal about 6.5 months. All objections to expert qualifications or testimony (F.R.E. 701–706 and Daubert) are due with dispositive motions, about 4 months before trial, or are waived; responses about 3 months before trial, and replies are not required. Motions to exclude expert testimony styled as motions in limine will not be entertained. If a Daubert motion is filed, file the challenged expert’s report at least 7 days before the Daubert hearing.

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Scheduling order: motions and pretrial disclosures
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Scheduling order: motions and pretrial disclosures: Motions to amend or join parties about 29 weeks before trial; dispositive motions about 4 months before trial (untimely ones may be summarily denied). Motions in limine (non-expert) and other nondispositive motions about 60 days before trial; responses to motions in limine about 30 days before, and to other nondispositive motions 14 days after filing. Criminal motions in limine are due at least 15 days before trial unless otherwise set. 30 days before the final pretrial conference: final witness lists, exhibit lists, deposition designations, exhibit inspection, and damages lists; evidence depositions must be done. Written authenticity or admissibility objections are due 21 days before the conference or are waived. If the trial date moves, other dates not expressly tied to it stay. Civil trials

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Trial: The judge conducts preliminary voir dire and usually allows counsel to follow up; peremptory challenges go on a form. Opening time limits are set at the final pretrial conference; closing limits during trial. Stand and examine from the lectern; one attorney per witness, including objections. Keep sidebars to a minimum and raise issues at breaks. Give the courtroom deputy advance notice of video testimony, and at least 2 days’ notice to use the evidence presentation system. Move each exhibit in individually before publishing it, unless admitted by stipulation; raise known exhibit objections by the final pretrial conference. No examination beyond redirect and recross absent exceptional circumstances. To have the jury polled, ask at the pretrial conference and again promptly after the verdict.

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Criminal sentencing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Criminal sentencing (trap): To get an evidentiary hearing on a PSR objection, expressly request it when filing the objection or the response (L.R. 83.9(c)). A party presenting witnesses at sentencing must file a Notice (Other) at least 14 days before the hearing, giving each witness’s legal name and estimated testimony time; late notice may mean exclusion.

docs.t: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer (E.D. Tenn.) — Settlement and dismissal
docs.x: Judge Katherine Amber Crytzer, E.D. Tenn.. Settlement and dismissal: On a full settlement, promptly file a Notice of Settlement, then a Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(ii) stipulation signed by all parties who have appeared, including former parties (L.R. 68.1). When seeking dismissal, identify which provision of Rule 41 applies. In employment discrimination cases, a joint report on suitability for the Federal Mediation Program is due about 5.5 months before trial. Default and default judgment requests should use the court’s posted procedures and forms.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Dispositive motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Dispositive motions (trap): Except on subject matter jurisdiction, each party generally gets one dispositive motion per stage (one motion to dismiss, one summary judgment motion), one supporting memorandum per motion, and one response to each opposing motion. The limits apply per party, not per counsel; consolidated or joint responses are encouraged. Statements of undisputed material facts are not required and will not be considered unless jointly submitted. Factual assertions without proper record citation will not be considered. A dispositive motion does not stay discovery; motions to stay are granted only in unusual circumstances.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Page limits and replies (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Page limits and replies (trap): Local Rule 7.1(b) limits exclude the cover sheet, tables of contents and authorities, and certificate of service. Noncompliant briefs may be disregarded or the motion summarily denied. Move to exceed sufficiently before the brief is due; such motions are rarely granted absent compelling reasons. Replies are not required (L.R. 7.1(c)); if one becomes necessary, it may not exceed 10 pages.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Communications and hearings
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Communications and hearings: The preferred communication is a formal motion filed on ECF. Anything conveyed by phone or email from chambers or clerk’s staff is not part of the record and does not bind the court. Copy all parties on any correspondence. Ex parte contact with staff is strongly discouraged; any contact must go to dumitru_chambers@tned.uscourts.gov, avoid the merits, and include all counsel of record. In-person conferences and hearings are strongly preferred; request telephonic participation well in advance by email. To request oral argument, file a separate motion with a memorandum of no more than 5 pages; the court gives weight to requests that give a young lawyer a chance to argue. Courtesy copies are not required unless requested; any paper copies must be bound, collated, and double-sided. Email proposed orders in Word to chambers.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Scheduling conference and ESI
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Scheduling conference and ESI: Be ready to discuss reasonable deadlines under Rule 16; counsel’s input gets significant weight. Before the conference, agree as far as possible on an ESI protocol covering sources and search limits, form of production, preservation, inadvertently produced privileged ESI, and cost allocation, and be ready to argue any disagreement. Extensions are entertained only if they do not affect the trial date or the court’s ability to decide dispositive motions, and must be sought by motion before the deadline, with the movant showing necessity. If the trial date changes, other dates stay in place.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery (trap): Discovery and all related motion practice must be completed by the deadline; serve requests early enough that responses and objections are resolved before it. The parties may continue by agreement afterward, but the court will not address disputes arising after the deadline. Bring disputes promptly, preferably by motion specifying the relief sought. If all parties agree a phone conference would avoid motion practice, request one by email to chambers. Per the form order, any Daubert motion must be filed before the discovery deadline, and the court should be told early if a Daubert hearing may be needed.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Form scheduling order deadlines
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Form scheduling order deadlines: Counted back from trial: plaintiff’s experts 21 weeks, defendant’s 17 weeks, rebuttal within 30 days after defendant’s; joinder and amendment 17 weeks; final witness list and notice on mediation 15 weeks; discovery 13 weeks; dispositive motions 11 weeks; pretrial disclosures (filed and served) 9 weeks; motions in limine 4 weeks; jury instructions 3 weeks; final pretrial conference no later than 2 weeks. Objections to designations and exhibits, and counter-designations, are due within 10 days after service. Also within 10 days of the pretrial disclosures, jointly submit (not file) electronic full deposition transcripts with each side’s designations highlighted in different colors, and electronic copies of all exhibits numbered continuously across parties with a master list. Disclose courtroom technology to the other side

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Motions in limine
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Motions in limine: Each party files a single motion listing all in limine issues with one brief of no more than 25 pages; the response is limited to 25 pages and any reply to 10. The court may reserve ruling until the issue arises at trial.

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Jury instructions and findings
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Jury instructions and findings: File one set of joint proposed jury instructions, verdict forms, and interrogatories 3 weeks before trial, covering each claim, defense, element, burden, standard of proof, and type of relief, with authority; email Word copies to chambers. Phased trials need separate sets for each phase. For disputed items, each side submits its version with a brief, supported explanation; an item submitted in only one version is assumed agreed. Follow the form of the Sixth Circuit Pattern Jury Instructions, and certify that you conferred to resolve differences. Bench trials: proposed findings and conclusions with authority (L.R. 52.1) are due 4 weeks before trial, with facts in chronological order and conclusions stating elements, burden, standard, and remedy without argument; email them in WordPerfect or a compatible format.

Trial conduct (trap): Counsel appear at 9:00 a.m. for preliminary matters; trial starts at 9:30 a.m. Stand at the lectern to examine, never approach a witness without permission, and never stand near or lean on the jury box. Jurors may not question witnesses. Counsel may lead voir dire within limits, then submit challenges on the deputy’s form; no back-striking of previously seated jurors. Share any visuals, video, or audio for openings with opposing counsel before trial. Only one lawyer per side may examine and object during a given witness. Sidebars are discouraged; raise matters during breaks. Resolve the method for recorded testimony with the other side before trial. Know Local Rule 43.3 and give the deputy 3 copies of the exhibit list before trial. Stipulated exhibits need not be moved in individually. Exhibits that can be electronic must be, and j

docs.t: Judge Mike J. Dumitru (E.D. Tenn.) — Jury deliberations and settlement
docs.x: Judge Mike J. Dumitru, E.D. Tenn.. Jury deliberations and settlement: Jurors may take notes during the proof but not openings or closings. During deliberations, give the deputy a mobile number and be able to return within 10 minutes. The deputy polls on request, and post-verdict juror contact will not be permitted absent extraordinary circumstances. Mediation or other ADR is urged in every case. Tell the court immediately upon settlement, and file a stipulation or agreed order of dismissal within 30 days or by the trial date, whichever is sooner.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Scheduling (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Scheduling (trap): Scheduling orders are entered directly, without an in-person conference. Questions about the trial date go to the judicial assistant within 7 days of receiving the order; after that, a motion for continuance is required. Any schedule change requires a motion with a proposed agreed order; continuances need cause, and successive resettings need compelling necessity. If the trial date moves, all other dates stay unless the court orders otherwise. The form order counts back from trial: amendments, joinder, and all Rule 12 and Rule 56 motions due 150 days before (untimely dispositive motions may be summarily denied); employment discrimination cases file a joint mediation-suitability report at 150 days.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Communications and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Communications and courtesy copies: Written correspondence is discouraged; copy all counsel if you send it. No courtesy hard copies unless the court asks; any requested copy must be printed after e-filing so it bears the ECF header. If you file on the day of a hearing or trial, notify chambers or the courtroom deputy by email or phone.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Hearings and page limits
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Hearings and page limits: Oral argument is decided case by case, and the court may set argument on its own. Follow Local Rule 7.1(b) page limits; reasonable requests to exceed them may be granted in complex cases.

docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Status report and pretrial order (trap): A joint status report is due on the discovery deadline, covering completion of discovery, whether argument would help on pending dispositive motions, planned pretrial motions, jury or nonjury and trial length, settlement and mediation, and other matters. Plaintiff serves a draft pretrial order 45 days before trial (47 if by mail); defendant responds within 5 working days. If no agreement after a face-to-face conference, plaintiff notifies chambers at least 31 days before trial. The agreed pretrial order is due 30 days before trial; failure may be treated as failure to prosecute.

docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Pretrial filings: Final witness lists 45 days before trial (supplement within 5 days after service). docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Trial: Counsel arrive at 8:30 a.m. for preliminary matters; trial begins at 9 a.m. A case not reached is held in line for that week. Bring the original and one copy of labeled, numbered exhibits. The judge conducts preliminary voir dire and allows counsel to follow up; challenges go on a form, and back-striking is not permitted. docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Closing arguments (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Closing arguments (trap): Agree on time limits before closings and follow them strictly. Stay within arm’s length of the DEPS podium and no closer to the jury than its jury-side edge; remove flip-chart pages after use. Objections during closing must state only the legal ground. Refer to witnesses by proper names, not first names alone (unless commonly so called at trial), refer to opposing counsel only as “Plaintiff’s counsel” or “Defendants’ counsel,” and show no reaction to opposing argument.

docs.t: Judge Thomas A. Varlan (E.D. Tenn.) — Injunctions and settlement
docs.x: Judge Thomas A. Varlan, E.D. Tenn.. Injunctions and settlement: TROs and injunctions follow Rule 65; briefing as in other cases, and expedited discovery on motion. docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Summary judgment (trap): File a separate, concise statement of material facts in numbered paragraphs, each supported by no more than two record citations. No argument in these statements; failure to file one may lead the court to strike the motion or opposition.

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Communications and conferences
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Communications and conferences: Written correspondence is discouraged; if sent, copy all counsel. Law clerks may be contacted, but not on the merits. docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Facts go in chronological order as proved at trial; conclusions must be concise and not argumentative.

docs.t: Judge Thomas W. Phillips (E.D. Tenn.) — Injunctions, ADR, and criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Thomas W. Phillips, E.D. Tenn.. Injunctions, ADR, and criminal cases: Rule 65 is strictly applied, and extraordinary relief is granted only in extraordinary circumstances. Expedited discovery requires compelling circumstances and may not be used in cases that clearly do not qualify for Rule 65 relief. Mediation, arbitration, and other ADR are encouraged, and reasonable extensions to pursue them are usually granted. In criminal cases, the assigned magistrate judge controls pretrial preparation; trial practice is the same as in civil cases.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Summary judgment (trap): Statements of undisputed facts are not required and will not be considered unless jointly submitted; follow Rule 56’s record-citation standards instead. Before any summary judgment motion, the parties must confer and build a single joint appendix of exhibits, consecutively paginated with a table of contents, filed by the movant with the first motion and cited by page number. Include only cited deposition pages. The non-movant may add a consecutively numbered addendum with its opposition. Material outside the appendix and addendum will not be considered. Each party gets only one motion to dismiss and one summary judgment motion (jurisdictional issues excepted), one supporting memorandum per motion, and one response per opposing motion; consolidated or joint responses are encouraged.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Briefing limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Briefing limits (trap): Replies are not required (L.R. 7.1(c)); any reply is capped at 10 pages, and only the first 10 pages of a longer reply will be considered. Requests for 5 extra pages in opening and answering briefs are typically granted in sufficiently complex cases but rarely for replies; move at least 10 days before the brief is due, if the schedule allows. Extension motions must be filed well before the deadline and specifically define the reasons for and length of the extension. Contacting a law clerk does not extend any deadline; only a timely motion can.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Hearings and communications
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Hearings and communications: Oral argument is set when the court finds it useful. To request it, file a separate motion with a memorandum of no more than 5 pages; the court weighs whether argument offers a speaking opportunity for a young lawyer. At scheduled hearings, be ready to present evidence; failing to arrange it is no ground for a continuance. Emergency (Rule 65) hearings are often set the same day the petition is filed; pre-hearing briefing is welcome. Correspondence may not substitute for motions and must be copied to all parties. To speak with a law clerk, email mcdonough_chambers@tned.uscourts.gov explaining why, with a callback number. No printed courtesy copies unless requested.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Case management conference
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Case management conference: The court usually holds an in-person case-management conference at the start of each case. Every lawyer who will actively handle discovery, motions, or trial must attend in person, ready to discuss legal theories, disputed facts, anticipated evidence, and the Rule 16(a) and 16(c)(2) topics. Out-of-district lawyers are encouraged to use local counsel. Typical deadlines before trial: expert disclosures, joinder, and amendments 29 weeks; rebuttal experts 25 weeks; final witness list 23 weeks; discovery close 19 weeks; dispositive and Daubert motions 15 weeks; pretrial disclosures 6 weeks; motions in limine 5 weeks; jury instructions or proposed findings 3 weeks; final pretrial conference the Monday two weeks before trial. Discovery typically takes about 8 months. A dispositive motion does not stay discovery, and stays a

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Discovery: Confer before raising disputes; leave from a magistrate judge is not needed to file a discovery motion. Do not contact the opposing side’s experts. Rebuttal experts may only challenge the opinions or methods of a previously disclosed expert, no broader in scope. Discovery, including evidence depositions, expert depositions, and requests for admission, must be completed by the cut-off. Confidentiality agreements bind the parties, but sealing requires Local Rule 26.2 and the sealing order entered at the start of the case.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Motions in limine and Daubert (trap)
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Motions in limine and Daubert (trap): Each party may file only one motion in limine identifying all evidence to be excluded, with one brief of no more than 25 pages; separately filed motions in limine will be summarily denied. Attach the challenged evidence where practicable. Motions to exclude expert testimony under Rule 702 must be filed by the Daubert deadline; they will not be entertained as motions in limine.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Final pretrial conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Final pretrial conference (trap): The final pretrial conference (3 p.m., Courtroom 3, Chattanooga) must be attended in person. Submit an agreed final pretrial order following the posted sample by the conference; it supplants the pleadings, so include your jury demand to avoid a waiver argument. File trial briefs on anticipated evidentiary and legal issues at least 3 business days before the conference. Before the conference, file an exhibit list and provide pre-marked exhibits, and be ready to argue admissibility; unprepared counsel risk adverse rulings. Jury instructions are submitted as one joint proposal, with competing versions of unresolved instructions, all with citations (L.R. 7.4), and emailed to chambers.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Trial (trap): Counsel lead voir dire under the court’s direction: for-cause challenges first, then peremptories; jurors called later are seated at the end of the box, and no back-striking. Openings and closings rarely exceed 30 minutes per party. Share any visual, video, or audio aids with opposing counsel before use. Examine from the lectern, standing if able; one attorney per witness for questioning and objections. Offer each exhibit when it is authenticated and its admissibility established, not at the end of testimony or of your case. Give the courtroom deputy three copies of the exhibit list before trial. No vouching, testifying, or ad hominem attacks in closing. All exhibits that can be electronic must be; jurors view them electronically, and firearms and controlled substances stay out of the jury room. During deliberations, be able to re

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Criminal cases: Plea and motion deadlines set by the magistrate judge are enforced unless modified by motion to the court. Be ready to justify appeal or § 2255 waivers in Rule 11(c)(1)(A) or (B) agreements. Brady material is deemed requested at the defendant’s first appearance with counsel, and the government should disclose exculpatory and mitigating information as soon as practicable; early Jencks production is encouraged. Rule 17(c)(1) pretrial subpoenas require a motion, filed well before the plea deadline and trial.

docs.t: Judge Travis Randall McDonough (E.D. Tenn.) — Settlement and referrals
docs.x: Judge Travis Randall McDonough, E.D. Tenn.. Settlement and referrals: Tell the court immediately upon settlement and promptly file a stipulation or agreed order of dismissal, in any event before the trial date (L.R. 68.1). Social Security and ERISA dispositive motions are typically referred to a magistrate judge for a recommendation.

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Contacting chambers (trap)
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Contacting chambers (trap): Before calling chambers with a case question, review the docket and the Local Rules, and have the docket available during the call. Only requests for settlement conferences and status conferences may be made by faxed letter; a status-conference request must briefly state the reason. Everything else requires a written motion, and chambers staff cannot grant relief by phone.

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Confidential position papers and status updates
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Confidential position papers and status updates: Send confidential position papers, and status updates only when directed by the court or staff, to EWD_Com@lamd.uscourts.gov as PDF attachments formatted under the Local Rules. Nothing else may be emailed there, and ex parte email communication is not permitted.

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Proposed orders and judgments
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Proposed orders and judgments: Proposed orders go with the e-filed motion (last page or attachment) and must also be emailed in an editable format such as Word to ewd_orders@lamd.uscourts.gov with the case number in the subject line. Proposed judgments, when ordered, are emailed in Word and not filed in CM/ECF; subject line “Proposed Judgment - [case number] EWD.”

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Diversity jurisdiction: citizenship (trap)
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Diversity jurisdiction: citizenship (trap): The Notice applies to complaints and notices of removal (and the citizenship parts to Rule 7.1(a)(2) statements) in cases assigned to the judge that invoke 28 U.S.C. § 1332; the court screens all new filings. Allege an individual’s domicile and citizenship, not residence; both state of incorporation and principal place of business for a corporation; and every member of an LLC or partnership by name, through all layers. Negative allegations (“not a citizen of Louisiana”) are insufficient, and intervenors’ or joined parties’ citizenship must be alleged when leave is sought. If a non-named party removes claiming to be the correct defendant, allege citizenship of both it and the named defendant. Failure to establish citizenship of all parties requires remand.

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Diversity jurisdiction: amount in controversy on removal (trap)
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Diversity jurisdiction: amount in controversy on removal (trap): Usually sufficient: a petition with an art. 893 statement or an affirmative over-$75,000 allegation (or wrongful-death/survival claims); a good-faith pre-removal demand over $75,000 (for a “policy limits” demand, proof the plaintiff knew the limits); an unequivocal discovery admission; or records showing damages over $75,000. Without such evidence, these are insufficient in personal-injury removals: conclusory statements, boilerplate damage categories, general injury descriptions, disc or spinal diagnoses and treatment without documented medical expenses over $25,000, no art. 893 statement, refusal to sign a damages stipulation, or citing other cases’ awards. In insurance-contract cases, policy limits or unquantified damage allegations generally don’t suffice; use an over-$75,000 demand o

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Pretrial order
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Pretrial order: Plaintiff’s counsel prepares the Pretrial Order with all parties’ cooperation, signed by all counsel; a party disagreeing with any part attaches an Opposition before submission. It covers jurisdiction, pending motions, each party’s claims, established facts, exhibits, witnesses, proposed amendments, settlement or ADR possibilities, jury or non-jury status, and each side’s time estimate. For each exhibit state only whether authenticity is objected to and why; admissibility objections go by motion in limine and pretrial memoranda on a schedule set at the pretrial conference. Absent good cause, only listed exhibits and witnesses are allowed.

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Witnesses and depositions at trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Witnesses and depositions at trial (trap): Will-call witnesses must be produced or subpoenaed and kept available, and a party may not release one without the other side’s express written or on-the-record consent. Designate deposition portions for the court and all parties no later than 21 days before trial. Video depositions are capped at 30 minutes and read depositions at 30 pages; file a written transcript of any video deposition into evidence, and supply a reader for any transcript read. Edit objections out of the tape or transcript; deposition objections needing a ruling are due to the court 14 days before trial.

docs.t: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes (M.D. La.) — Jury instructions and courtroom (trap)
docs.x: Judge Erin Wilder-Doomes, M.D. La.. Jury instructions and courtroom (trap): Joint jury instructions, including a joint verdict or interrogatory form, are filed by the scheduling-order deadline. No separate filings are allowed: disagreements go in footnotes with case authority and pinpoint citations. Fifth Circuit pattern instructions may be cited by number and edition. Courtroom 5 is fully electronic; present exhibits by laptop or document camera, and arrange training before trial with courtroom deputy Brandy Lemelle Route (the notice lists (225) 389-3584; the page lists (225) 389-3588 for the deputy).

docs.t: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles (M.D. La.) — Exhibits attached to filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Exhibits attached to filings (trap): Any pleading, motion, memorandum, opposition, or brief that attaches exhibits must include, as a separate CM/ECF attachment, an Exhibit List giving the caption, a descriptive title, the exhibit numbers or letters, and a description of each exhibit. File each exhibit separately; no in globo exhibits (attachments to affidavits and depositions may stay with them but must be shown on the list). Each exhibit’s docket description must match the Exhibit List. This division rule controls over any conflicting Administrative Procedures.

docs.t: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles (M.D. La.) — Proposed orders, judgments, and contact
docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Proposed orders, judgments, and contact: Proposed orders go with the e-filed motion (last page or attachment) and must also be emailed in an editable format, preferably Word, to jwd_orders@lamd.uscourts.gov with the case number in the subject line. Proposed judgments, when ordered, are emailed in Word and not filed in CM/ECF; subject line “Proposed Judgment - [case number] JWD.” The page reminds counsel, quoting old Spanish law once in force in Louisiana, that a lawyer who intentionally miscited the law could be exiled and have property confiscated. Media must not contact the courtroom deputy, docket clerk, or chambers.

docs.t: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles (M.D. La.) — Pretrial order (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Pretrial order (trap): Plaintiff’s counsel prepares the Pretrial Order with all parties’ cooperation, signed by all counsel, after conferring on stipulated facts, eliminating uncontested claims, and exchanging trial exhibits. If a party won’t cooperate, call chambers (225-389-3568); a party disagreeing with any content attaches an Opposition before submission. For each exhibit state whether there are authenticity objections and why; admissibility objections are raised instead by motions in limine and pretrial memoranda on a schedule set at the pretrial conference. Exhibits must be pre-marked and Bates stamped, with a Bench Book copy ready on a date set at the conference. Will-call witnesses must be produced or subpoenaed and available to the other side even if not called; may-call witnesses need not be. Absent good cause, only claims, exhibits, a

docs.t: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles (M.D. La.) — Jury instructions and verdict forms (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Jury instructions and verdict forms (trap): 28 days before every civil jury trial, submit one joint proposed draft of the final charge after a good-faith effort to agree. Disputed instructions are numbered and embedded where desired, each with a footnote stating the objection and the proponent’s response; the court aims to circulate a draft charge ruling on the objections before trial. Confer on a verdict form; if no agreement, separate forms may be filed, highlighting the agreed interrogatories, and pocket briefs of no more than 5 pages on the other side’s form are due within 7 days. Objections may be preserved at the charge conference. The older Uniform Pretrial Notice allows separate filings on disputed items and lets Fifth Circuit pattern instructions be cited by number and edition.

docs.t: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles (M.D. La.) — Impeachment evidence (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Impeachment evidence (trap): To use documents or evidence solely for impeachment that are not on the Pretrial Order or not exchanged in discovery, file a motion for leave to file a sealed motion for in-camera inspection no later than 30 days before trial, attaching the evidence and briefly explaining what it impeaches and how. (The Uniform Pretrial Notice says simply to submit it under seal for in camera inspection by the same deadline.)

docs.t: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles (M.D. La.) — Depositions at trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Depositions at trial (trap): Designate the portions of written or video depositions to be read or shown no later than 28 days before trial, after conferring and redacting irrelevant and redundant material, including colloquies between counsel. Only necessary portions may be used. Motions in limine on deposition objections are due 21 days before trial and must identify each objected-to question by page and line with a concise objection. Give the courtroom deputy redacted transcripts at trial, and supply a reader for any transcript to be read.

docs.t: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles (M.D. La.) — Voir dire and bench trials
docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Voir dire and bench trials: Each party submits proposed voir dire questions; to question the panel directly, state the reasons and estimate the time needed. The judge’s posted standard voir dire covers eligibility, juror cards, panel questions, case-specific questions, and party questions only “as approved by Court”; the court reads a brief case description circulated to the parties before trial. In non-jury trials only, submit proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law.

docs.t: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles (M.D. La.) — Exhibits and courtroom technology
docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Exhibits and courtroom technology: Each party submits an Electronic Bench Book through CM/ECF (Utilities / Evidence Upload) before trial or evidentiary proceedings, at the time set in the order; it is for the court only. Name files by exhibit number, part, and description (e.g., “1-a_photograph.jpg”), mark sealed exhibits “SEALED,” note redactions, and keep files under 500MB (split video into 10-minute clips). JERS is not used by counsel to present evidence: use a laptop connection or the document camera in Courtroom 1, and keep trial exhibits matching the uploaded numbers and images. Arrange equipment training with courtroom deputy Kristie Causey (225-389-3574) before trial. Admitted exhibits stay with the offering party until appeal time runs (L.R. 79).

docs.t: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles (M.D. La.) — Settlement affidavit
docs.x: Judge John Wheadon deGravelles, M.D. La.. Settlement affidavit: By the scheduling-order deadline, counsel for each party files an affidavit stating the date and time of a settlement conference of counsel. Plaintiff’s counsel attests to a good-faith offer and conveying the counteroffer; defense counsel attests to conveying the offer and making a good-faith counteroffer. State no dollar amounts. The Pretrial Order must also state the settlement history and whether the parties want a settlement conference before a magistrate judge, plus jury or non-jury status and each side’s time estimate.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Scheduling and contact
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Scheduling and contact: No standard days or times for any matter, except Nashville jury trials, which start Tuesdays at 9:00 a.m. Courtroom 6C; courtroom deputy (615) 736-7157. Correspondence with the court is discouraged; when permitted, serve it on opposing counsel, and it will be filed as public record (confidential settlement statements excepted). No telephone calls with the law clerks. Requests to take part in case management or other conferences by telephone must be made in advance by written motion.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Chambers copies
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Chambers copies: Judge Trauger does not want chamber copies of filings unless the judge requests them.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Case management
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Case management: Judge Trauger holds the initial case management conference personally. File a joint proposed initial case management order 3 business days before it, and lead counsel for all parties must attend. With rare exceptions, a firm trial date is set at the initial conference and will not be moved. Pro se cases go to a magistrate judge for case management. The sample order calls for a Joint Mediation Report saying whether the parties will mediate and, if so, the mediator and date.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Extensions and continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Extensions and continuances (trap): Agreed extensions are routinely granted, except for dispositive motion deadlines; trial continuances are rarely granted. Make requests in writing and state opposing counsel’s position if possible.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Motions and briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Motions and briefing (trap): Briefs may not exceed 25 pages. Replies are optional on dispositive motions; on other motions, replies need leave. Under the sample order, responses to dispositive motions are due 21 days after filing and optional replies 10 days after the response. No partial summary judgment motion without leave: first file a separate motion justifying it in terms of overall economy of time and expense. Oral argument is granted when appropriate or beneficial. Dispositive motions are not referred to the magistrate judge, except in pro se cases.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Discovery (trap)
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Discovery (trap): 40 interrogatories, including subparts (the sample order expands Local Rule 33.01(b)). No discovery motion may be filed until the parties have conferred in good faith and then scheduled and taken part in a conference call with Judge Trauger. Where a magistrate judge is managing the case, that judge resolves discovery disputes, and most discovery motions are referred. Discovery is not stayed during dispositive motions unless ordered. Protective orders and confidentiality agreements are considered case by case.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Expert testimony in writing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Expert testimony in writing (trap): In civil cases and some criminal cases, expert testimony (other than medical) must be reduced to writing before trial and is read at trial as the expert’s direct testimony. Departures are considered case by case. Challenge an expert’s qualifications by motion in limine.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — TROs
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. TROs: TRO papers must state efforts made to contact the other side. The judge deciding the TRO may not be the assigned judge; for a TRO sought after the case starts, advise the presiding judge’s secretary. Expedited discovery requires a written motion showing good cause.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Pretrial
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Pretrial: An agreed proposed pretrial order is due no later than the pretrial conference; contents and timing are set in the order setting the case for trial. Pretrial briefs are not routinely required in jury cases. Motions in limine must be filed and answered before the pretrial conference, per the trial order’s deadlines; the judge tries to rule on them at the conference. Requests to accommodate out-of-town parties, witnesses, or lawyers go by written motion at the earliest opportunity or at a pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Trial: Trial days run 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. with a one-hour lunch; no trailer dockets for civil trials. After the court’s voir dire, counsel question the whole panel; peremptory strikes are made simultaneously on written forms (duplicate strikes possible), and cause challenges at the bench. Exhibits must be premarked; show each to opposing counsel first and have an extra copy for the court. Give exhibit and witness lists to the court, deputy, reporter, and opposing counsel on day one. Juror copies are allowed with advance notice. File agreed jury instructions in hard copy and on disk, one per page with a heading, and disputed ones with citations, by the deadline set at the pretrial conference. No interim commentary by counsel; only one lawyer may examine a given witness. Raise matters outside the jury’s presence at recesses. The judge polls the ju

docs.t: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger (M.D. Tenn.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Aleta Arthur Trauger, M.D. Tenn.. Criminal cases: A pretrial conference is set once it is clear the case will be tried. Do not assume a trial continuance will be granted. Notify the courtroom deputy by phone or email as soon as a plea is decided and suggest timing; deliver the drafted plea petition, any plea agreement, and the government’s statement of elements and penalties to chambers before the plea.

docs.t: Judge Chip Frensley (M.D. Tenn.) — Chambers and contact
docs.x: Judge Chip Frensley, M.D. Tenn.. Chambers and contact: Email proposed case management orders to frensleychambers@tnmd.uscourts.gov. No chambers copies of filings unless the judge requests them. Correspondence, other than for scheduling, is discouraged; any permitted letter must be served on opposing counsel and is filed as public record unless directed otherwise. Contact law clerks only for scheduling questions and never about the merits. Requests for out-of-town counsel to appear by phone must be made by motion well in advance. Telephone conferences are not recorded (the judge usually enters an order reciting the outcome); a record requires an in-court proceeding.

docs.t: Judge Chip Frensley (M.D. Tenn.) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Chip Frensley, M.D. Tenn.. Discovery disputes (trap): Counsel must actually talk about the disputed issues before raising them, and the LR 37.01(b)(3) certification must say they have spoken. A motion to compel, for protective order, or for sanctions will be denied if counsel have not spoken, or if it is uncertain whether they have. Raise unresolved disputes promptly by requesting a telephonic discovery conference or by motion; either way the parties must file a joint discovery dispute statement describing the specific requests and each side’s position with facts and authority. Motions to compel or for protective order must address Rule 26(b)(1) proportionality. No speaking objections at depositions; state objections concisely (“hearsay,” “a conclusion”) without argument. Raise needs for more or fewer than 25 interrogatories at a case management conference or by motion.

docs.t: Judge Chip Frensley (M.D. Tenn.) — Case management orders

A motion to amend must attach the proposed amended pleading as an exhibit and state whether it is opposed, after discussing it with all counsel.

docs.t: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr. (M.D. Tenn.) — Sealing and protective orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr., M.D. Tenn.. Sealing and protective orders (trap): A motion to seal (L.R. 5.03 and 7.01), even if unopposed, must show compelling reasons and narrow tailoring and analyze each document in detail with facts and citations. Typically only trade secrets, privileged material, and information confidential by statute qualify. Proposed protective orders may not provide that “confidential” discovery is automatically sealed when filed or used at trial; such language will be stricken and may sink the motion. Protective orders must comply with Sixth Circuit authority.

docs.t: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr. (M.D. Tenn.) — Experts, ESI, and AI
docs.x: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr., M.D. Tenn.. Experts, ESI, and AI: In civil cases and some criminal cases, expert testimony (other than medical) must be reduced to writing and exchanged before trial and is read at trial as direct testimony (L.R. 39.01(c)(5)(E)); departures are considered case by case. Challenge qualifications by motion in limine. Rebuttal experts only by leave; untimely supplemental expert opinions may be excluded. Any ESI agreement must be in writing and filed within 14 days of the initial case management conference; otherwise Administrative Order No. 174-1’s defaults apply. The sample order reminds attorneys who use generative AI of their Rule 11(b) and 26(g) and ethical duties to verify citations and propositions.

docs.t: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr. (M.D. Tenn.) — Case resolution
docs.x: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr., M.D. Tenn.. Case resolution: About 14 days after fact discovery closes, file a joint report confirming a good-faith attempt to resolve the case and stating whether ADR might help. A request for a judicial settlement conference must explain why mediation is not feasible, propose timing, and state any preferred magistrate judge.

docs.t: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr. (M.D. Tenn.) — Pretrial
docs.x: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr., M.D. Tenn.. Pretrial: Submit a joint proposed pretrial order before the pretrial conference containing: a statement that it supplants the pleadings, jurisdiction, each side’s theory (1 page maximum each), the issues (marking jury and court issues), relief sought, anticipated evidentiary disputes, and estimated trial length. Motions in limine must comply with L.R. 7.01(a)(1) and be filed and answered before the pretrial conference, where the judge tries to rule on them. Give notice of an anticipated JMOL motion no later than the pretrial conference, with a brief.

docs.t: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr. (M.D. Tenn.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr., M.D. Tenn.. Trial: Trial days run 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. with a one-hour lunch. After counsel’s voir dire, cause challenges are made at the bench, then peremptory strikes simultaneously on written forms. Exhibits must be premarked numerically and placed in binders, each party’s set in a different color. Show exhibits to opposing counsel first and have an extra copy for the court; exhibit and witness lists go to the court, deputy, reporter, and opposing counsel on day one. Juror copies of admitted exhibits need advance notice. File agreed jury instructions and email a copy to the courtroom deputy, one per page with a heading; file disputed instructions with citations by the same deadline. No interim commentary; only one lawyer may examine a given witness. Raise matters outside the jury’s presence at recesses. The judge polls the jury in every case.

docs.t: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr. (M.D. Tenn.) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge William Lynn Campbell Jr., M.D. Tenn.. Criminal cases: A status conference is set about 45 days before trial and a pretrial conference about 1 week before. A motion to continue trial must be filed with a Waiver of Speedy Trial Rights signed by the defendant. Notify the courtroom deputy by phone or email as soon as a plea is decided and suggest timing; deliver the drafted plea petition, any plea agreement, and the government’s statement of elements and penalties to chambers before the plea.

docs.t: Judge Benita Y. Pearson (N.D. Ohio) — Generative AI disclosure (trap)
docs.x: Judge Benita Y. Pearson, N.D. Ohio. Generative AI disclosure (trap): Any party, pro se or represented, who uses a generative AI tool to prepare a filing must disclose in the document that AI was used and which tool, and certify that the filer checked the accuracy of every AI-drafted portion, including all citations and legal authority. Failure to disclose and certify can bring sanctions including striking the filing, filing restrictions, monetary sanctions, and dismissal.

docs.t: Judge Benita Y. Pearson (N.D. Ohio) — Pre-motion demand before dispositive motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Benita Y. Pearson, N.D. Ohio. Pre-motion demand before dispositive motions (trap): Before filing a Rule 12(b), 12(c), or 56 motion, a party must send opposing counsel a written request to be dismissed or for judgment. Opposing counsel must agree or give explicit written reasons for refusing; the movant must then reassess, and any motion must include a statement certifying that this exchange occurred. Defendants must answer even if they have filed or plan to file a motion to dismiss or for judgment; the motion does not delay the answer deadline. Lead counsel must confer in person to prepare written stipulations of uncontested facts for dispositive motions, filed by the court-set date (or a joint notice that there are none). These are mandatory.

docs.t: Judge Benita Y. Pearson (N.D. Ohio) — Motions and briefing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Benita Y. Pearson, N.D. Ohio. Motions and briefing (trap): Page limits under LR 7.1(f) are strictly enforced. A motion to exceed them must show good cause and be filed far enough ahead for a ruling; one filed with the overlength memorandum will be denied. Only a motion and memorandum, an opposition, and a reply are allowed; no sur-replies without advance leave. Motions for reconsideration should not be filed routinely or as a reflexive response to an adverse ruling. Motions to amend: the amendment cutoff is not blanket leave. Absent written consent, file a motion for leave with a memorandum addressing Rule 15(a), and certify that prior notice of the proposed amendment was given and consent withheld.

docs.t: Judge Benita Y. Pearson (N.D. Ohio) — Case management conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Benita Y. Pearson, N.D. Ohio. Case management conference (trap): The CMC is telephonic; plaintiff’s counsel sets up the call and calls chambers at (330) 884-7435 with all participants on the line. Lead counsel and parties must personally participate (for an entity, the person most familiar with the facts, plus a representative with full settlement authority where an insurer is involved). A motion to excuse attendance or to continue the CMC is due at least 14 days before it and must include three agreed proposed dates. Rule 26(f) conference at least 21 days before the CMC; the planning report is due at least 5 days before. Plaintiff must make a written itemized damages demand at least 14 days before the CMC, and defendant must respond in writing with an offer (even if none) at least 7 days before; note both in the report. Initial disclosures are due and certified to the court 14 day

docs.t: Judge Benita Y. Pearson (N.D. Ohio) — Discovery
docs.x: Judge Benita Y. Pearson, N.D. Ohio. Discovery: LR 37.1 is vigorously enforced: after good-faith efforts fail, give the court informal notice with a certification of the effort, by letter or a call to chambers with both sides on the line. File a discovery motion only when the court solicits it. Do not file discovery materials unless used in the proceeding. When relying on deposition testimony, the court prefers the entire deposition to excerpts, filed with the memorandum it supports. Telephone calls to chambers are limited to scheduling or as the Local Rules allow; the court speaks through its docket, so requests must be made by written motion.

docs.t: Judge Benita Y. Pearson (N.D. Ohio) — Protective orders and sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Benita Y. Pearson, N.D. Ohio. Protective orders and sealing (trap): A proposed stipulated protective order (Appendix L form) will be rejected unless it requires a party using “confidential” material on a motion to file that material under seal, and binds the parties before and after entry. Materials used in open court at trial lose the confidential designation. On a motion to dismiss or for summary judgment, only the supporting confidential documents, not the motion itself, may be filed under seal.

docs.t: Judge Benita Y. Pearson (N.D. Ohio) — Civil final pretrial and trial filings
docs.x: Judge Benita Y. Pearson, N.D. Ohio. Civil final pretrial and trial filings: Lead trial counsel and parties with full settlement authority must attend the final pretrial conference unless excused on written motion. Trials are set on a two-week stand-by basis; counsel must keep in touch with the courtroom deputy (330-884-7435) for the exact date. By 4:00 p.m. 10 days before trial: an agreed preliminary statement for the jury, joint voir dire, jury instructions, interrogatories, and verdict forms (one joint filing: agreed, plaintiff’s opposed, and defendant’s opposed, all with citations), and trial briefs. Witness and exhibit lists 3 business days before trial; unlisted witnesses and exhibits are excluded absent good cause. Stipulated facts: plaintiff circulates a draft 14 days before the pretrial conference, responses at 10 days, meet at 7 days, and file the signed final stipulation 3 days

docs.t: Judge Benita Y. Pearson (N.D. Ohio) — Exhibits and courtroom conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge Benita Y. Pearson, N.D. Ohio. Exhibits and courtroom conduct (trap): Exhibits go to chambers on a separate CD, DVD, or USB drive per side (and one for joint exhibits), received by noon the Friday before trial, named like “12_2009 Tax Statement.pdf” (numeric exhibit number, underscore before any description). Paper exhibits must bear numbered stickers with the case number, and every page of a multi-page exhibit is separately numbered (e.g., Plaintiff 1-1). Binders are no longer required. Exchange demonstratives 2 days before trial. Trial runs 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday; arrive 30 minutes early. Stand to address the court and examine from the lectern, state only the legal basis for objections, use surnames, and only one lawyer per side per witness (the lawyer objecting on direct takes cross). Video-conference witnesses need a docketed notice at least 1 week before

docs.t: Judge Benita Y. Pearson (N.D. Ohio) — Continuances and settlement
docs.x: Judge Benita Y. Pearson, N.D. Ohio. Continuances and settlement: No trial or hearing is continued without a written motion stating the reason (in civil cases, endorsed by all moving parties and lead counsel). A motion based on a conflicting trial assignment must attach it (criminal: describe it) and be filed within 15 days after learning of the conflict and at least 30 days before trial. Report a settlement immediately by calling 330-884-7435; failure can draw sanctions, and jury costs are assessed under LR 54.1 if settlement comes after a jury is called.

docs.t: Judge Benita Y. Pearson (N.D. Ohio) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Benita Y. Pearson, N.D. Ohio. Motions to travel filed within 48 hours of the travel will be denied and must state whether the AUSA objects. Discovery requests are docketed as “Notices” unless court intervention is needed; report any discovery failures in writing on the cutoff date. By 4:00 p.m. 10 days before trial, the same jury materials and trial briefs as civil (briefs may be ex parte). Witness lists go to the court, not to the other side, 3 business days before trial; written stipulations, si

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Motion to dismiss does not stop the case (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Motion to dismiss does not stop the case (trap): A timely Rule 12(b) motion to dismiss does not excuse an answer, discovery, or compliance with other orders. The answer is due the same day as plaintiff’s opposition to the motion. Exceptions: a motion challenging personal jurisdiction, or a stay sought and granted while the motion is pending. Then the motion is decided first, and if it is denied in whole or part the answer is due 20 days after the order.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Pre-CMC substantive motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Pre-CMC substantive motions (trap): Substantive motions filed before the Case Management Conference (e.g., to dismiss, for judgment on the pleadings, to confirm or vacate an arbitration award, to remand): opening memorandum and response 20 pages each, response due within 30 days of the motion; reply 10 pages, due within 14 days of the response. After a motion for a more definite statement is granted, the responsive pleading is due within 14 days of notice of the order, or the pleading may be stricken. No sur-replies without advance leave.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Briefing format and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Briefing format and page limits (trap): One-inch margins; double-spaced 12-point Times New Roman; footnotes at least 10-point Times New Roman; citations in the text, not footnotes. All filings, and exhibits if possible, must be text searchable. Noncompliant filings may be stricken or deemed untimely. Excessive or lengthy footnotes may be treated as evading page limits, with the brief or footnotes stricken. Relief from page limits needs a separate motion filed well before the deadline, showing good cause, the extra pages sought, and all parties’ positions. A request filed with the overlength brief will be denied, and the brief may be stricken or treated as ending at the last permitted page.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Continuances and extensions
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Continuances and extensions: Motions to continue or extend must be in writing, well in advance, and (unless joint) state whether they are opposed. Requests made after a submission, discovery, or dispositive-motion deadline has passed are denied absent excusable neglect. For an unopposed motion to continue a conference or hearing, propose three alternative dates and times when all counsel are available.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Discovery disputes (trap): Meet and confer in person, by video, or by phone first; email never suffices. If unresolved, jointly notify chambers by phone (216-357-7200) or email (Brennan_Chambers@ohnd.uscourts.gov); the court will set a call and may require a certificate of compliance stating how the parties conferred. A discovery motion filed without these steps will be denied. Serve requests early enough that responses are due before the cut-off, and raise disputes early enough to finish by the deadline. Discovery the parties agree to continue past the cut-off gets no court supervision absent extreme prejudice and will not move dispositive-motion or trial dates.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Summary judgment
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Summary judgment: Typically one summary judgment motion per party. No summary judgment motion before the close of discovery without express leave.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Sealing and redactions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Sealing and redactions (trap): Seek leave before filing anything redacted, usually at least 7 days before the deadline: explain each redaction, certify conferral with the producing party and state its position, and simultaneously give the court an unredacted copy with proposed redactions marked. Sealing an entire document is permitted only rarely. Justify every request document by document under Shane Group, Inc. v. Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan, 825 F.3d 299 (6th Cir. 2016); a confidentiality designation under a protective order is not enough. A protective order deviating from Appendix L to the Local Rules requires emailing chambers a redlined Word version of the changes; joint proposals are viewed more favorably.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Hearings, conferences, and attendance (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Hearings, conferences, and attendance (trap): Conferences and hearings are in person unless the court says otherwise. A request for phone or video must be filed at least 7 business days ahead; joint requests are liberally granted. Lead counsel, client representatives with full settlement authority, and insurance representatives must attend hearings and conferences in person, except the CMC, telephonic status conferences in the scheduling order, and discovery-dispute status conferences. A request to excuse attendance must be in writing at least 7 calendar days ahead. File a joint status report 3 business days before any status conference covering discovery, settlement, whether a mediator would help, and anticipated discovery issues. Only lead counsel need attend a telephonic status conference.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Removal and jurisdictional declarations (trap)
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Removal and jurisdictional declarations (trap): In a diversity removal, if the pleadings or notice of removal do not identify the citizenship of every member or partner of each LLC, LLP, partnership, or similar party, counsel must file a declaration within 14 days of the notice of removal (corporations: State of incorporation and principal place of business). Missing the deadline risks sanctions or remand. An entity intervenor in a diversity case must file the same citizenship declaration with its motion to intervene, plus the corporate disclosure statement.

docs.t: Judge Bridget M. Brennan (N.D. Ohio) — Rule 26(f) report and ESI
docs.x: Judge Bridget M. Brennan, N.D. Ohio. Rule 26(f) report and ESI: Use the judge’s Report of Parties’ Planning Meeting form, which calls for initial disclosures no later than 5 business days before the CMC, a track recommendation, ADR position, and a proposed telephonic status conference at least one month before the close of fact discovery. If the parties have not agreed on an ESI method by the time the report is filed, the default standard in Appendix K to the Local Rules applies.

docs.t: Judge Charles E. Fleming (N.D. Ohio) — Artificial intelligence ban (trap)
docs.x: Judge Charles E. Fleming, N.D. Ohio. Artificial intelligence ban (trap): No attorney or pro se party may use artificial intelligence in preparing any filing. Violations can bring sanctions including striking the filing, economic sanctions or contempt, and dismissal of the lawsuit. The ban does not cover information gathered from legal search engines (such as Westlaw or LexisNexis) or internet search engines (such as Google). Parties and counsel must immediately tell the court if they discover AI use in any document filed in their case.

docs.t: Judge Charles E. Fleming (N.D. Ohio) — Deadlines expire at 5 p.m. (trap)
docs.x: Judge Charles E. Fleming, N.D. Ohio. Deadlines expire at 5 p.m. (trap): Unless otherwise ordered, every court-set filing deadline expires at the close of business, meaning 5:00 PM on the deadline date. Anything later is late and may be stricken, not considered, or sanctioned.

docs.t: Judge Charles E. Fleming (N.D. Ohio) — Continuances and extensions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Charles E. Fleming, N.D. Ohio. Continuances and extensions (trap): No hearing is continued and no deadline extended without a written motion stating the reason, filed before the date or deadline passes; a motion based on a conflict must be filed as soon as counsel learns of the conflict. Every such motion (except one joined by all parties) must state whether the other parties oppose. An opposed motion must be filed at least 7 days before the date or deadline, and the opposition is due within 3 days after the motion is filed. Noncompliance may mean denial.

docs.t: Judge Charles E. Fleming (N.D. Ohio) — Motions and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Charles E. Fleming, N.D. Ohio. Motions and page limits (trap): Motions and briefs must follow Loc. R. 7.1 unless ordered otherwise. No supplemental motion, document, sur-reply, or exhibit for or against a dispositive motion is accepted without prior leave unless the case management order addresses it. Length limits under Loc. R. 7.1(f) are strictly enforced. A motion to exceed them must show good cause and be filed at least 7 days before the filing deadline; one filed together with the overlong memorandum will be denied.

docs.t: Judge Charles E. Fleming (N.D. Ohio) — Formatting
docs.x: Judge Charles E. Fleming, N.D. Ohio. Formatting: All filings must meet Loc. R. 10.1, and e-filed documents (including exhibits, if possible) must be text-searchable. Nonconforming documents may be stricken.

docs.t: Judge Charles E. Fleming (N.D. Ohio) — Sealing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Charles E. Fleming, N.D. Ohio. Sealing (trap): Nothing is filed under seal without statutory authority or a court order. Seek leave first, explaining the basis and stating whether other parties oppose; if the document is tied to a deadline, the motion for leave is due at least 7 days before it. Sealing a whole document or exhibit is permitted only rarely. Justify every redaction or sealing request under Shane Grp., Inc. v. Blue Cross Blue Shield of Mich., 825 F.3d 299 (6th Cir. 2016), analyzing each document in detail with reasons and legal citations.

docs.t: Judge Charles E. Fleming (N.D. Ohio) — Disclosure statements
docs.x: Judge Charles E. Fleming, N.D. Ohio. Disclosure statements: Nongovernmental corporate parties and would-be intervenors must disclose any parent corporation and any publicly held corporation owning 10% or more of their stock, or state that none exists. In diversity cases (including removed cases), every party and intervenor must name and establish the citizenship of everyone whose citizenship is attributed to it; an LLC must identify the name and citizenship of each member and every sub-member. Allegations of residence rather than domicile or citizenship are insufficient (Prime Rate Premium Fin. Corp. v. Larson).

docs.t: Judge Charles E. Fleming (N.D. Ohio) — Contacting chambers
docs.x: Judge Charles E. Fleming, N.D. Ohio. Contacting chambers: Direct case questions to Courtroom Deputy Clerk Stephanie Siner at (216) 357-7180. Do not contact the law clerks about the case. Routine calls (such as dial-in information) are acceptable. For a deposition dispute needing immediate help, the parties may call chambers jointly.

docs.x: Judge Christopher A. Boyko, N.D. Ohio. Dispositive motions and extensions (trap): Unscheduled summary judgment motions may not be filed without leave. docs.x: Judge Christopher A. Boyko, N.D. Ohio. Status reports: If the case management order requires them, file status reports every 45 days covering discovery, settlement discussions, pending motions, and any developments that might prompt a request to deviate from the schedule. docs.x: Judge Christopher A. Boyko, N.D. Ohio. Discovery disputes and protective orders (trap): Follow Local Rule 37.1. docs.t: Judge Dan Polster (N.D. Ohio) — Motions and briefing (trap)

docs.t: Judge Dan Polster (N.D. Ohio) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Dan Polster, N.D. Ohio. Trial: Trial runs 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. with a 1-hour lunch and two 15-minute breaks (the practices page says 5:00 p.m.); counsel must be in the courtroom from 8:30 a.m. Parties must be present whenever the jury is seated. The court conducts voir dire, then one counsel per party briefly questions the panel (about 10 minutes per party). Peremptories use an “informed strike” method by rounds; a pass forfeits that challenge, and consecutive passes by both sides end challenges. Examinations need not be from the lectern; ask permission to approach a witness. Show any opening-statement exhibits to opposing counsel in advance. Jurors may take notes and submit written questions. Raise Daubert challenges well before trial, and arrange daily transcripts.

docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. docs.t: Judge Donald C. Nugent (N.D. Ohio) — Remote testimony and courtroom technology
docs.x: Judge Donald C. Nugent, N.D. Ohio. docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Motion practice (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Motion practice (trap): Parties on the same side must file one joint brief (noting any argument a party does not join), and the opponent files one response. For cross-motions the court prefers a four-brief schedule (opening; combined cross-motion and response; combined response and reply; reply). No surreplies without leave, rarely given. Replies should not raise new evidence or arguments. Notices of supplemental authority may not exceed 350 words and must cite a PageID or point argued orally. Motions for reconsideration, however styled, are limited to 2 pages (or 500 words) or will be struck; no response unless the court asks. docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Pleadings, jurisdiction, and dismissals (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. docs.t: Judge J. Philip Calabrese (N.D. Ohio) — Depositions (trap)
docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Depositions (trap): Local Rule 30.1 is strictly enforced. Objections are limited to “Objection, Form” or “Objection, Foundation” unless the questioner asks for the reason or privilege is asserted. Interjections such as “if you know” or “if you remember” are treated as coaching. Don’t interrupt answers, repeat or paraphrase prior testimony (defending counsel’s repetition counts as a speaking objection), or mislead the witness. Evasive answers are treated as a failure to testify and may bring an additional deposition; yes-or-no questions get yes, no, or a statement that they can’t be answered that way. Agreements to change the 7-hour limit are enforced only if in writing; 7 hours means on the record, excluding breaks.

docs.x: Judge J. Philip Calabrese, N.D. Ohio. Sealing an entire document is allowed only rarely. A confidentiality designation under a protective order is not enough; the movant must justify sealing document by document under Shane Group. Once approved, file the redacted version, serve the unredacted version, and file it under seal.

docs.x: Judge Jack Zouhary, N.D. Ohio. Summary judgment pre-motion letters (trap): No summary judgment motion may be filed until counsel meet and confer and exchange letters. The judge then discusses the motion and, if appropriate, sets a briefing schedule. More generally, no dispositive motion may be filed until counsel confer on its merits and enough discovery is done for the movant to represent there are no disputed material facts; timing must not disrupt the case schedule or trial date.

docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio.
