Brief any Daubert issues before filing for summary judgment; the judge will decide them promptly first. If a motion turns on an unresolved, dispositive question of Ohio (or another state’s) law, ask the court to consider certification to that state’s supreme court before briefing.

docs.t: Judge James G. Carr (N.D. Ohio) — Reconsideration (trap)
docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio. Reconsideration (trap): Motions for reconsideration are strongly disfavored. A motion that merely challenges the court’s reasoning or has no plausible justification draws sanctions of the greater of $2,000 or the prevailing party’s actual fees and costs.

docs.t: Judge James G. Carr (N.D. Ohio) — Discovery disputes
docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio. Discovery disputes: Discovery may start before the CMC by agreement, and counsel may agree to exceed the federal and local discovery limits without a motion for leave. After a good-faith conference (need not be in person), notify chambers, preferably by email, with a brief description; the judge personally handles discovery disputes, including during depositions. No privilege log unless ordered; disputed documents under 40 pages may be submitted under seal at least 3 business days before the conference. Do not end a deposition without first contacting chambers. No speaking objections, rudeness, or profanity; resolve email delays by phone.

docs.t: Judge James G. Carr (N.D. Ohio) — CMC, TROs, and filing
docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio. CMC, TROs, and filing: The CMC is usually set earlier than the Local Rules timetable. Ideally meet and confer and file a Report of the Parties’ Planning Meeting a week before. A TRO applicant must make all reasonable efforts to identify defense counsel and send them the complaint, motion, and brief, unless notice would jeopardize plaintiff’s interests. Everything must be filed text searchable, including depositions and critical exhibits. Pro hac vice admission may be moved orally at the CMC or another pretrial conference if no one objects.

docs.t: Judge James G. Carr (N.D. Ohio) — Settlement conferences (trap)
docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio. Settlement conferences (trap): Usually by Zoom, hosted by chambers. Lead trial counsel must participate, and entity representatives need full authority, meaning authority to settle up to the opposing party’s final pre-conference demand. Referral to Magistrate Judge Clay or others is available on request. Plaintiff’s good-faith demand is due 3 weeks before; defendant’s offer 2 weeks before; each side files an ex parte narrative settlement statement 1 week before (strengths and weaknesses of each side, last demand/offer, and what the client will accept or pay). The judge routinely asks parties to agree to binding, non-appealable resolution by the judge of post-settlement disputes and to retained jurisdiction.

docs.t: Judge James G. Carr (N.D. Ohio) — Continuances and pretrial deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio. Continuances and pretrial deadlines (trap): The trial date is firm; counsel may not stipulate to move it or make other substantive schedule changes. Modest changes that do not disrupt filing deadlines or trial may be made with advance notice to the courtroom deputy. Motions in limine 2 weeks before trial, oppositions 1 week before. Witness lists (in calling order) and marked exhibits exchanged 1 week before trial; plaintiff uses numbers, defendant letters, one per exhibit. Technology or special exhibit needs to the deputy 2 weeks before trial. Proposed jury instructions (substantive only, with sources) and special verdicts are due 1 week before trial after the parties confer. Preference: Sixth Circuit pattern, then Devitt & Blackmar, then Sand; Ohio law from Ohio Jury Instructions. Trial briefs only if requested.

docs.t: Judge James G. Carr (N.D. Ohio) — Civil trial
docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio. Civil trial: Trials run Tuesday through Friday, with voir dire usually the Monday afternoon before. Be available at 8:15 a.m.; trial runs to 4:30 or 5 p.m. At day’s end, tell the court and opposing counsel the next day’s witnesses, exhibits, and expected length, and raise objections then. A magistrate judge may conduct voir dire on consent; counsel participate. Cause challenges at sidebar immediately after the juror’s questioning; peremptories alternate outside the jury’s presence. Twelve jurors usually deliberate. Before each witness, briefly summarize the testimony. Objections are brief with the rule cited; no speaking objections, and argument is at sidebar. Show exhibits to opposing counsel before displaying them. Jurors may ask screened questions if all counsel agree.

docs.t: Judge James G. Carr (N.D. Ohio) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge James G. Carr, N.D. Ohio. Criminal cases: Surety bonds are strongly disfavored; propose alternatives such as third-party custody, property bonds, or location monitoring. No appraisal or financial documentation is needed to post property. Rule 16, Jencks, and Brady discovery motions are usually unnecessary. For motions needing an evidentiary hearing (e.g., suppression), file a brief statement of grounds; legal briefing follows the hearing. Other motions must be fully briefed; counsel may exceed Local Rule page limits. Sentencing memoranda are due 10 days before sentencing, filed under seal, with typewritten (not handwritten) attachments. The judge considers a blanket refusal to let the defendant meet with Probation inappropriate. No post-trial contact with jurors outside the courthouse without court approval.

docs.t: Judge James R. Knepp II (N.D. Ohio) — Case management conference
docs.x: Judge James R. Knepp II, N.D. Ohio. Case management conference: The CMC is held in Chambers 318, 1716 Spielbusch Avenue, Toledo. Parties need not attend unless ordered. Local counsel must attend in person or arrange telephone participation by calling chambers (419-213-5570); out-of-town counsel may arrange to participate by phone. If settlement talks would help at the CMC, tell chambers so extra time can be set aside and party attendance secured. Counsel should be ready to discuss claims and defenses in detail.

docs.t: Judge James R. Knepp II (N.D. Ohio) — Rule 26(f) report and early discovery
docs.x: Judge James R. Knepp II, N.D. Ohio. Rule 26(f) report and early discovery: Plaintiff’s counsel arranges the Rule 26(f) meeting; a jointly signed report substantially in the court’s form is due at least 3 days before the CMC. The form asks for the recommended track, ADR suitability, magistrate-judge consent, e-discovery issues (with a reminder of the Appendix K default standard), and proposed amendment, expert, discovery, and dispositive-motion dates. All Rule 26(a) disclosures apply, on a date agreed by counsel or set at the CMC. Absent agreement, no formal discovery before the CMC except as needed for jurisdictional challenges or emergency, temporary, or preliminary relief. Local Rule 30.1 governs deposition conduct.

docs.t: Judge James R. Knepp II (N.D. Ohio) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge James R. Knepp II, N.D. Ohio. Discovery disputes (trap): No motion to compel, for a protective order, or for sanctions may be filed unless the parties have tried in good faith to resolve the dispute and then contacted the court by phone or email to request judicial resolution. Local Civil Rule 37.1 governs. The standard CMC order provides that inadvertent disclosure of privileged or work-product material does not waive protection in this or any other proceeding (Evidence Rule 502(d)).

docs.t: Judge James R. Knepp II (N.D. Ohio) — Filing discovery
docs.x: Judge James R. Knepp II, N.D. Ohio. Filing discovery: Without leave, discovery material is not filed except as needed to support dispositive motions. Filed depositions must include the Word Index.

docs.t: Judge James R. Knepp II (N.D. Ohio) — Settlement conferences (trap)
docs.x: Judge James R. Knepp II, N.D. Ohio. Settlement conferences (trap): Settlement conferences are held before Judge Knepp in Chambers 318. Parties and lead trial counsel must appear; a person with ultimate settlement authority must be personally present, and an insurer that will decide settlement must send a representative in person with full authority. Failing to bring the right people can bring fees, costs, or other sanctions. The conference usually starts with opening presentations, then joint discussion and private caucuses. Statements made are not to be used in discovery and are inadmissible at trial. Counsel must give clients a copy of the order and review it with them beforehand.

docs.t: Judge James R. Knepp II (N.D. Ohio) — Settlement exchanges and statements (trap)
docs.x: Judge James R. Knepp II, N.D. Ohio. Settlement exchanges and statements (trap): Plaintiff sends a written itemized damages demand with a brief explanation 14 days before the conference; defendant responds with a written offer 7 days before. If no settlement results, plaintiff’s counsel emails the settlement positions to chambers 3 days before the conference. Each party emails a confidential settlement statement to Knepp_Chambers@ohnd.uscourts.gov 3 days before the conference (not filed): facts, legal analysis, strengths and weaknesses, settlement position and latest proposal, and efforts to date, with critical documents not already in the file.

docs.t: Judge James S. Gwin (N.D. Ohio) — Attendance at every proceeding (trap)
docs.x: Judge James S. Gwin, N.D. Ohio. Attendance at every proceeding (trap): The judge’s page states that counsel of record, all parties, and a representative with settlement authority must attend every scheduled proceeding. For the case management conference, status conference, and final pretrial, “party” means the named individual or, for an entity, the person most familiar with the facts, not in-house counsel or someone who merely has settlement authority. “Final authority” means the ability to settle without further consultation up to the plaintiff’s prayer for relief (unlimited if no prayer is stated or equitable relief is sought). If that representative cannot attend in person, file a motion showing good cause more than 48 hours before the conference.

docs.t: Judge James S. Gwin (N.D. Ohio) — Filing format (trap)
docs.x: Judge James S. Gwin, N.D. Ohio. Filing format (trap): All documents must be filed as text-searchable PDFs and all exhibits specifically identified; otherwise the Clerk’s Office will mark a filing error and you must refile. Motions, memoranda, and all other documents must use only 12-point text.

docs.t: Judge James S. Gwin (N.D. Ohio) — Case management conference
docs.x: Judge James S. Gwin, N.D. Ohio. Case management conference: Report directly to Chambers 18A. The agenda follows Local Rule 16.3(b)(2). Discovery must start before the Rule 26(f) conference. Plaintiff’s counsel arranges the planning meeting, and a jointly signed report (substantially in the form attached to the order) is due electronically at least 3 days before the CMC; it must address ESI by agreeing on a method or adopting Appendix K. Objections to initial disclosures go in that report. A party expecting to seek attorney fees must file, at or before the CMC, a preliminary estimate or budget of fees and costs broken down by category (investigation and complaint, procedural motions, discovery, dispositive motions, settlement, trial, depositions, experts, witness fees, and other). If the case resolves before the CMC, file a jointly signed stipulation of settlement or dismissal or tell the

docs.t: Judge James S. Gwin (N.D. Ohio) — Motions and summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge James S. Gwin, N.D. Ohio. Motions and summary judgment (trap): An answer is required even if a motion to dismiss is filed or planned; the motion does not extend the answer deadline. Dispositive memoranda must come with an affidavit stating the case track and certifying compliance with the page limit (10 Expedited, 20 Standard or Administrative, 30 Complex, 40 Mass Tort). Limits are raised only in extraordinary circumstances. Only one summary judgment motion per party; further or supplemental motions need leave, granted only in very rare circumstances. File it on or close to the dispositive motion deadline. Record materials supporting a motion (e.g., deposition transcripts) should be excerpted to the relevant portion plus no more than 2 pages of context, though full transcripts may be e-filed. Deposition excerpts supporting or opposing a dispositive motion are attached as exhibits t

docs.t: Judge James S. Gwin (N.D. Ohio) — Experts and Daubert (trap)
docs.x: Judge James S. Gwin, N.D. Ohio. Experts and Daubert (trap): Under the Expert ID Order, parties identify experts (name and CV) by the dates set, exchange expert reports at least 90 days before trial, and give the court copies of the reports. Daubert objections to an expert’s qualifications must be filed 2 months before the standby trial date or are waived. Responses are due within 7 consecutive days.

docs.t: Judge James S. Gwin (N.D. Ohio) — Final pretrial
docs.x: Judge James S. Gwin, N.D. Ohio. Final pretrial: Counsel must meet at least 10 days before the pretrial conference to explore stipulations. A joint proposed stipulation and final pretrial order (in the Appendix A format, covering claims, uncontroverted facts, contested issues, witnesses, expert limits, depositions, exhibits, pending motions, and settlement status) is due electronically at least 3 days before the conference, with witness lists (name and synopsis of testimony). Deposition testimony to be used at trial must be filed by the final pretrial with the portions to be read marked; opponents may read omitted portions.

docs.t: Judge James S. Gwin (N.D. Ohio) — Civil trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge James S. Gwin, N.D. Ohio. Civil trial (trap): Cases are set on a two-week standby period; stay in regular contact with the courtroom deputy for the actual start date. Trial days run 8 a.m. to about 5 p.m. with a lunch break of about 30 minutes. Witnesses are presumed to be called in list order unless a revised order is given 48 hours ahead. Adding witnesses needs a motion and an offer of proof to the opponent at least 3 days before trial. Over-schedule witnesses: running out on any trial day is treated as resting. Each party submits all exhibits on a separate USB, CD, or DVD, received in Chambers 18A by noon the Friday before trial, using the file-naming convention -_.. All parties label exhibits with numbers (“Plaintiff 1,” “Def 2”) plus the case number, and bring two binder copies with an index on the morning of trial. The older Track Assignment version instead calls for one copy

docs.t: Judge James S. Gwin (N.D. Ohio) — Jury and bench submissions (trap)
docs.x: Judge James S. Gwin, N.D. Ohio. Jury and bench submissions (trap): Proposed voir dire questions are due 1 week before the standby trial period; late questions are waived. Proposed jury instructions are due 1 week before trial (later only for unforeseeable issues, at least 24 hours before closing), each on a separate 8½ x 11 sheet labeled “Plaintiff(s)/Defendant(s) Requested Instruction No. __” with a citation of authority, or it will be rejected. Sources include Sixth Circuit pattern instructions, O’Malley, Grenig and Lee (5th ed.), and Ohio Jury Instructions. Bench trials: a statement of issues, proposed findings (citing witnesses and evidence), proposed conclusions (citing authority), and any trial briefs are due 1 week before the standby period, and must be exchanged.

docs.t: Judge James S. Gwin (N.D. Ohio) — Trial time limits
docs.x: Judge James S. Gwin, N.D. Ohio. Trial time limits: In some cases a Trial Time Order allots each side a set number of minutes for its case (voir dire excluded) and up to 30 minutes for openings. Interim arguments are capped at 2 minutes and do not count against the time. Motions for more time may be made orally no sooner than halfway through the allotted time, and the court weighs how the time has been used. Under that order, trial runs from 8 a.m. with a 30–40 minute noon recess, ending between 4 and 5 p.m., and an eight-person jury may be seated.

docs.t: Judge James S. Gwin (N.D. Ohio) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge James S. Gwin, N.D. Ohio. Criminal cases: Pretrial and jury trial are in Courtroom 18A. Motions must include memoranda with supporting citations or may be struck. Counsel exchange proposed written stipulations of fact at least 1 business day before trial or a motion hearing. Witness lists are due 1 week before trial; running out of witnesses is treated as resting. Exhibits follow the same USB/CD/DVD, naming, numbering, and two-binder rules as civil trials. Proposed voir dire and jury instructions (with reasons and authority) are due 1 week before trial. Continuances of trial dates are disfavored, and extensions to plead require a written motion and good cause. Interim argument is usually permitted.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey J. Helmick (N.D. Ohio) — Discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey J. Helmick, N.D. Ohio. Discovery disputes (trap): No discovery motion may be filed unless the parties have tried in good faith to resolve the dispute, as LR 37.1 requires. If good-faith efforts fail, email a joint letter to Helmick_Chambers@ohnd.uscourts.gov summarizing the dispute and the efforts to resolve it. Chambers will then contact counsel about next steps.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey J. Helmick (N.D. Ohio) — Filing format (trap)
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey J. Helmick, N.D. Ohio. Filing format (trap): All filings must be text-searchable PDFs, and every exhibit must be specifically identified. If exhibits are merged into a single PDF, each exhibit must be bookmarked. Noncompliant documents will be marked as filing errors by the Clerk’s Office and must be re-filed.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey J. Helmick (N.D. Ohio) — Case management conference
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey J. Helmick, N.D. Ohio. Case management conference: All local counsel, including those in the metropolitan area, must appear in person except in extraordinary circumstances; anyone needing to appear by phone should notify chambers as early as possible. Out-of-town counsel may participate by phone by calling chambers to arrange it at least 3 business days before the conference. Parties need not attend unless the notice says otherwise. Report scheduling conflicts to chambers as soon as they are discovered.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey J. Helmick (N.D. Ohio) — Rule 26(f) report
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey J. Helmick, N.D. Ohio. Rule 26(f) report: Use the judge’s Report of Parties’ Planning Meeting form, which covers initial disclosures, track, ADR suitability and timing, electronic discovery (with a reminder of the Appendix K default standard), expert discovery, liability and damages discovery deadlines, and proposed dates for dispositive motions, amendments, and a status or final pretrial settlement conference.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey J. Helmick (N.D. Ohio) — Magistrate judge consent
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey J. Helmick, N.D. Ohio. Magistrate judge consent: Parties consenting to a magistrate judge should contact chambers (419-213-5690) before the CMC; a consent form will issue for signature and the case will go to the magistrate judge for the CMC and all further proceedings.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey J. Helmick (N.D. Ohio) — Settlement conferences
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey J. Helmick, N.D. Ohio. Settlement conferences: The judge encourages settlement efforts; counsel may contact chambers to schedule a conference. Parties and counsel must appear in person, and counsel must submit a confidential ex parte settlement narrative to chambers 7 days before the conference.

docs.t: Judge John R. Adams (N.D. Ohio) — Motions and page limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge John R. Adams, N.D. Ohio. Motions and page limits (trap): Strictly follows Local Rule 7.1. Dispositive memoranda: 10 pages (expedited), 20 (standard and administrative), 30 (complex), 40 (mass tort); all other motions 15 pages. Leave to exceed is rarely granted and must be sought well before the deadline; a request filed with the overlength brief will be denied and does not extend the filing deadline. Motions are decided on the papers; oral argument is rare. Unopposed motions are not automatically granted. No sur-replies without advance leave. Emergency motions are rarely granted ex parte; notify the opposing party and give them a copy.

docs.t: Judge John R. Adams (N.D. Ohio) — Courtesy copies and contact
docs.x: Judge John R. Adams, N.D. Ohio. Courtesy copies and contact: No courtesy copies unless the court asks, except that papers not e-filed and due within 2 business days of a conference, hearing, or trial must be faxed to the court and opposing counsel the same day. The practices page asks for 2 courtesy copies of any motion or brief over 40 pages. No ex parte communications. Contact the courtroom deputy only on scheduling and miscellaneous matters, and law clerks only on procedure. Non-motion correspondence is discouraged and phone requests or inquiries are not appropriate; to request a non-discovery status conference, send a letter certifying a good-faith effort to resolve the issues.

docs.t: Judge John R. Adams (N.D. Ohio) — Extensions and continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge John R. Adams, N.D. Ohio. Extensions and continuances (trap): Extension requests must be filed at least 14 days before the deadline and are granted only in exceptional circumstances. Counsel’s stipulations do not extend Case Management Plan deadlines. Continuance requests for any appearance must be filed in writing at least 7 days ahead (the CMC order requires 14 days for the CMC, with three agreed alternative dates). Trial continuances are rare; in civil cases the motion must be signed by the parties and counsel.

docs.t: Judge John R. Adams (N.D. Ohio) — Case Management Conference
docs.x: Judge John R. Adams, N.D. Ohio. Case Management Conference: Held about 30 days after the answer. Lead counsel, parties with full settlement authority, and an insurer representative with full authority must attend with calendars; a motion to excuse attendance is due 14 days before. Initial disclosures 14 days before the CMC; jointly signed planning report 3 business days before (the practices page says faxed 3 days before). No formal discovery before the CMC except on jurisdiction or emergency relief. Plaintiff makes a written demand with a monetary damages breakdown 14 days before, defendant responds 7 days later, and both go in the report. If fees are claimable, each party brings a preliminary fee estimate/budget to the CMC. Magistrate-judge consent must be filed 14 days before the CMC.

docs.t: Judge John R. Adams (N.D. Ohio) — Status reports and conferences (trap)
docs.x: Judge John R. Adams, N.D. Ohio. Status reports and conferences (trap): Status reports are due every 45 days, starting 45 days after the Case Management Plan, covering discovery, settlement talks, motions, and anything that may require schedule changes. Failing to file one automatically forfeits the right to seek extensions, and repeated failures can lead to dismissal of claims or defenses. Before a status hearing or settlement conference, confer within 72 hours of it and fax (not file) a joint settlement report of no more than 2 pages at least 2 business days ahead (the practices page says 5 days) covering facts, discovery, the demand and offer, and issues for the court. Discovery disputes follow L.R. 37.1: good-faith effort, then a phone conference triggered by a short letter, then position letters if requested, then a Rule 37 motion. When relying on a deposition, the court prefers the

docs.t: Judge John R. Adams (N.D. Ohio) — Settlement conferences
docs.x: Judge John R. Adams, N.D. Ohio. Settlement conferences: Plaintiff sends a written damages itemization and demand at least 14 calendar days before; defendant responds with a written offer at least 7 calendar days before. If no settlement, plaintiff’s counsel delivers or faxes both letters to chambers by the date set; do not file them. Lead counsel and parties with ultimate authority must attend in person; insurers need authority up to the existing demand. Phone availability is allowed only in extenuating circumstances with leave at least 7 days ahead. Give the client a copy of the order and discuss it beforehand.

docs.t: Judge John R. Adams (N.D. Ohio) — Civil trial preparation (trap)
docs.x: Judge John R. Adams, N.D. Ohio. Civil trial preparation (trap): Stipulations of fact, a joint preliminary statement (2 pages max), trial briefs (facts, controlling law, evidentiary issues), witness and exhibit lists, proposed voir dire, and proposed findings and conclusions (bench trials) are due 10 calendar days before trial. Unlisted witnesses and exhibits are excluded absent good cause. Objections to witnesses or exhibits are due 5 days before trial. Motions in limine 14 days before trial, oppositions 7 days later. Designate deposition testimony 14 calendar days before trial, objections 7 days later; file a brief on unresolved objections with highlighted excerpts. Jury instructions: substantive law, damages, and interrogatories only. Exchange 10 calendar days before the final pretrial and file one joint submission (agreed, plaintiff-only, defendant-only, with citations) 1 business day

docs.t: Judge John R. Adams (N.D. Ohio) — Exhibits and trial day
docs.x: Judge John R. Adams, N.D. Ohio. Exhibits and trial day: Plaintiff’s exhibits start at 1, defendant’s at 1001, with the case number on the sticker; number each page of multi-page exhibits (Pl. Ex. 1-1). More than 10 exhibits go in tabbed binders with a table of contents; 2 copies to chambers 2 business days before a civil trial (criminal: 1 copy the morning of trial). Trial runs 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (the practices page says 5 p.m.) with a one-hour lunch and two 15-minute breaks; counsel must be present 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. for matters outside the jury’s presence. Parties arrange daily transcripts. The judge conducts extensive voir dire, then may allow brief supplemental questioning. Peremptories are by round; a pass forfeits that challenge, and consecutive passes end challenges. Stipulations used by the jury must be written and signed. Raise possible Daubert challenges well before trial.

docs.t: Judge John R. Adams (N.D. Ohio) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge John R. Adams, N.D. Ohio. Criminal cases (trap): Plea agreements are not accepted after the date of the pretrial conference; plea agreements go electronically to the deputy or law clerk 1 business day before a plea hearing. Written pleas are strongly preferred. Pretrial motions are due 30 days after arraignment (later only with leave), responses within 7 days; pro forma motions are disfavored. Trial briefs, exhibit lists, motions in limine, and proposed voir dire are due 7 business days before trial, with objections 3 days later. Witness lists go to chambers by email (not filed or exchanged) 3 business days before trial. Signed stipulations (counsel and defendant), the joint preliminary statement, and the joint jury instructions (filed and hand-delivered or faxed, plus an editable electronic copy) are due 3 business days before trial. Jencks material is strongly encouraged by the c

docs.t: Judge John R. Adams (N.D. Ohio) — Social Security appeals
docs.x: Judge John R. Adams, N.D. Ohio. Social Security appeals: Automatically referred to a magistrate judge on the Administrative Track. The order directs that the Report and Recommendation be filed within 6 months of the transcript, and in any event within 285 days of the answer and transcript.

docs.t: Judge Michael Hendershot (N.D. Ohio) — Word limits and brief format (trap)
docs.x: Judge Michael Hendershot, N.D. Ohio. Word limits and brief format (trap): The judge prefers word counts to page limits. Word-limit equivalents to Local Rule page limits: 10 pages = 3,500 words, 20 = 7,000, 30 = 11,000, and 40 = 15,000; letter briefs 500 words and amicus briefs 5,000. A brief using word limits must certify compliance, and every brief except a letter brief needs a table of contents and a table of authorities. Use at least 12-point proportionally spaced font (footnotes included) and preferably 1.25-inch margins. Footnotes are disfavored and citations in footnotes strongly disfavored. Use party names, not procedural labels, in titles and text; text-searchable PDFs and hyperlinks are preferred. Motions to exceed the limits or to file a sur-reply will almost never be granted. Parties on the same side must file jointly (noting any party that does not join an argument) and may t

docs.t: Judge Michael Hendershot (N.D. Ohio) — Record citations and exhibits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Michael Hendershot, N.D. Ohio. Record citations and exhibits (trap): Every cite to a deposition, exhibit, or similar material must give the ECF record number and PageID number, so file the materials first (for example, before a summary judgment motion) to generate PageIDs. Give exhibits descriptive names (“Doe Depo.” rather than “Exhibit ZZ”), strip old ECF headers from previously filed documents, and file PDFs of cited internet materials. Caselaw need not be attached unless it is unavailable on a court website, Westlaw, or LEXIS.

docs.t: Judge Michael Hendershot (N.D. Ohio) — Particular motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Michael Hendershot, N.D. Ohio. Particular motions (trap): One summary judgment motion per party without leave, and no cross-motion for summary judgment in response to another party’s motion absent an order. A motion in limine cannot substitute for summary judgment. Reconsideration is strongly disfavored and available only on Rule 59 or 60 grounds; a functional reconsideration motion and any response must be letter briefs. Notices of supplemental authority take letter-brief form, cite the affected pages or argument point, and may be answered by letter brief within 10 days. Dismissing fewer than all parties or claims requires a Rule 21 motion stating whether any party objects; a Rule 41 filing for that purpose will be stricken. Amicus briefs need no leave, are filed the same day as the supported party’s brief, and may be no longer than half that brief’s word limit (the word-limit tab

docs.t: Judge Michael Hendershot (N.D. Ohio) — Discovery disputes and deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Michael Hendershot, N.D. Ohio. Discovery disputes and deadlines (trap): Before any discovery motion: the filer must be complying with its own obligations, counsel must confer in person or by voice or video (and certify it), and then email Hendershot_Chambers@ohnd.uscourts.gov to schedule a conference; the court may then order letter briefs or full motions. Disputes must be raised at least 21 days before the discovery cut-off. Serve requests early enough that responses are due before the cut-off. Disclose lay trial witnesses at least 30 days before the discovery cut-off or they are barred absent good cause and extraordinary prejudice. Motions to change a discovery deadline should come at least 7 days before it. Boilerplate and general objections are treated as no objection; burden objections must be explained or quantified. An expert may consider only facts produced at least 60 days

docs.t: Judge Michael Hendershot (N.D. Ohio) — Deposition conduct (trap)
docs.x: Judge Michael Hendershot, N.D. Ohio. Deposition conduct (trap): Local Civil Rule 30.1 is strictly enforced. Defending counsel may say only “Objection, Form” or “Objection, Foundation” (unless instructing not to answer on privilege or asked for the reason); speaking objections and phrases like “if you know” or “if you remember” count as coaching. No interrupting answers, repeating questions, or misleading or mischaracterizing the witness. Evasive answers may be treated as a failure to testify and require a new deposition. Any agreement to change the seven-hour limit must be mutual, in writing, and state a specific reason.

docs.t: Judge Michael Hendershot (N.D. Ohio) — Rule 26(f) report and case management conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Michael Hendershot, N.D. Ohio. Rule 26(f) report and case management conference (trap): Exchange robust initial disclosures at least 7 days before the Rule 26(f) conference, or be ready to explain why at the CMC and make them within 14 days after it. The Rule 26(f) report, on the court’s form, is due at least 7 days before the CMC and must be signed by counsel and the parties (parties physically). It includes a disclosure addendum of litigation funders, insurers, and others with an interest in the case, which may be submitted ex parte by email to chambers. Preview any proposal for opposing counsel at least 3 days before any meeting with the court. Counsel must come able to make binding commitments on jurisdiction, key disputes, discovery scope, experts, ADR, and magistrate-judge consent; appearing without that authority counts as a failure to appear and can bring sanctions, dismiss

docs.t: Judge Michael Hendershot (N.D. Ohio) — Amended pleadings, sealing, and protective orders
docs.x: Judge Michael Hendershot, N.D. Ohio. Amended pleadings, sealing, and protective orders: A motion to amend or an amended pleading as of right must attach a track-changes copy and state whether the defendant consented under Rule 15(a)(2). A nonstandard protective order (not Appendix L) must be emailed to chambers in Word with a brief explanation of the variations. Redactions require leave sought 7 days before the filing is due, explaining each redaction with legal authority, stating the producing party’s position, and emailing chambers an unredacted copy with proposed redactions marked. If granted, file the redacted version, serve an unredacted copy, and file the unredacted version under seal. Sealing an entire filing is very rare.

docs.t: Judge Michael Hendershot (N.D. Ohio) — Scheduling, conferences, and contact
docs.x: Judge Michael Hendershot, N.D. Ohio. Scheduling, conferences, and contact: If a court-set conference or hearing conflicts with counsel’s or a necessary party’s schedule, confer and file a notice giving the reason and three alternative dates within two weeks before or after. This does not apply to trial dates, discovery cut-offs, or case-management-order dates. Request a status conference by motion listing every issue and each side’s position, after conferring. Calls and emails to chambers are limited to discovery issues and scheduling; all other requests go by written motion.

docs.t: Judge Michael Hendershot (N.D. Ohio) — Final pretrial and settlement (trap)
docs.x: Judge Michael Hendershot, N.D. Ohio. Final pretrial and settlement (trap): Lead trial counsel, the named parties (for corporations, the person most familiar with the case, not in-house counsel), and a representative with full settlement authority must attend the final pretrial conference in person; a motion to excuse attendance requires good cause and conferring, at least 3 days before. Exchange at least two rounds of good-faith demands and offers beforehand. If a settled case misses its dismissal deadline, the court may order an in-person hearing of counsel, parties, and those with settlement authority. ADR options include a private mediator, the assigned magistrate judge, or the court’s ADR Office.

docs.t: Judge Michael Hendershot (N.D. Ohio) — Fees, AI, and professionalism
docs.x: Judge Michael Hendershot, N.D. Ohio. Fees, AI, and professionalism: In fee-shifting and class actions, the fee claimant must give opposing counsel a running statement of fees and costs within 14 days after each calendar quarter ends, starting from the initial demand. Default judgment fee requests need lodestar support or will be denied. Anyone relying on AI-generated material must verify its facts and citations; filings with fake cases can bring sanctions up to dismissal or striking a defense, and anyone who spots possible AI errors must promptly tell the court. Zero tolerance for unprofessional conduct, including frivolous sanctions motions. The court invites proposals to give newer lawyers meaningful roles, such as splitting oral-argument time.

docs.t: Judge Pamela Barker (N.D. Ohio) — Meet-and-confer and discovery disputes (trap)
docs.x: Judge Pamela Barker, N.D. Ohio. Meet-and-confer and discovery disputes (trap): Any court-directed meet-and-confer must be in person, by video, or by phone; email is never enough to show good faith. For discovery disputes, comply with Local Rule 37.1, then (and only then) file Position Papers on the docket of no more than 5 pages excluding exhibits. Each must certify a sincere good-faith effort, attach the correspondence documenting the effort, and attach the requests, responses, and other relevant materials. No replies unless directed. Do not call or email chambers for help with a discovery dispute; everything goes on the docket. The one exception: a dispute during a deposition needing immediate help may be raised by a joint (never ex parte) call to chambers.

docs.t: Judge Pamela Barker (N.D. Ohio) — Contacting chambers (trap)
docs.x: Judge Pamela Barker, N.D. Ohio. Contacting chambers (trap): No ex parte calls to chambers on substantive issues, including case management deadlines, requests to file briefing, or the status of pending motions; file a motion on the public docket instead. Calls about routine matters (such as dial-in information) are acceptable.

docs.t: Judge Pamela Barker (N.D. Ohio) — Pleadings and protective orders
docs.x: Judge Pamela Barker, N.D. Ohio. Pleadings and protective orders: A partial Rule 12(b) motion to dismiss does not excuse filing an answer (due as calculated under Rule 12(a)) or complying with discovery; the case proceeds while the motion is pending. The judge strongly prefers the Appendix L protective order. To deviate, email a redlined Word version of the changes to Appendix L, with the reasons, to Barker_Chambers@ohnd.uscourts.gov; joint proposals are viewed more favorably.

docs.t: Judge Pamela Barker (N.D. Ohio) — Case management conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Pamela Barker, N.D. Ohio. Case management conference (trap): Lead counsel must attend the CMC in person in Room 16A. Motions to reschedule or excuse lead counsel’s in-person attendance are due at least 7 days before the CMC, and a motion to reschedule must propose at least 3 alternative dates agreeable to all after conferring; no calls or emails. Noncompliant requests are denied. Plaintiff’s counsel arranges the Rule 26(f) meeting (defendant’s counsel in removed cases); disclosures are due at or within 14 days after it, and the Report of Parties’ Planning Meeting is due at least 5 working days before the CMC. In ERISA cases there are no initial disclosures; counsel should instead follow the procedure in Wilkins v. Baptist Healthcare System and propose a briefing schedule. Patent cases use the Local Patent Rules report. A party expecting to seek attorney fees must file a preliminary

docs.t: Judge Pamela Barker (N.D. Ohio) — Motions, courtesy copies, and summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Pamela Barker, N.D. Ohio. Motions, courtesy copies, and summary judgment (trap): Send chambers a courtesy copy of all dispositive motions, oppositions, and replies with all supporting material (the patent and ERISA notices extend this to all briefing). No summary judgment motion before the close of discovery without express leave, and all summary judgment arguments must be in a single motion; multiple motions need leave. Under the CMC orders, dispositive-motion responses are due 30 days after service and replies 14 days after the response; no sur-replies without leave. Extension requests must be filed before the deadline and state whether opposing counsel consents. The court prefers that a party relying on deposition testimony file the entire deposition rather than excerpts (unless excerpts truly suffice), and supporting discovery materials must be filed with the memorandum.

docs.t: Judge Pamela Barker (N.D. Ohio) — Status and settlement conferences
docs.x: Judge Pamela Barker, N.D. Ohio. Status and settlement conferences: Before a status conference, counsel must confer within 5 business days of it about open issues and settlement positions, and within 3 business days of it send a joint status report or confidential individual reports (status of discovery, settlement positions, issues) by email to chambers; they need not be filed. The ERISA and older class-action CMC orders add settlement-conference terms: parties and lead counsel attend in person in Room 16A, with a person with knowledge and full authority for entities and an insurer representative if coverage is arguable; motions to excuse are due 7 days ahead. Within 5 days of the conference each side emails chambers a confidential settlement statement (negotiation status, positions, factual and damages outline), not filed or shared unless all parties request. If no ADR referral is made

docs.t: Judge Pamela Barker (N.D. Ohio) — Final pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Pamela Barker, N.D. Ohio. Final pretrial (trap): Parties and lead counsel must attend with full authority: for a plaintiff, to dismiss with prejudice and accept down to the defendant’s last offer; for a defendant, to pay up to the plaintiff’s last demand in the representative’s own discretion. Needing to call anyone to authorize an offer means the representative lacks full authority, and an insurer representative with full authority must attend when insurer approval is needed. Counsel must confer with their clients and each other on final settlement positions at least 2 business days before the final pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge Pamela Barker (N.D. Ohio) — Civil trial filings (trap)
docs.x: Judge Pamela Barker, N.D. Ohio. Civil trial filings (trap): Trial briefs are required from each party, filed and exchanged 10 days before trial with one copy delivered to chambers. They must include facts, controlling law (emphasizing possible Rule 50 issues), witnesses with subject matter, an exhibit index, evidentiary issues, and length estimate, plus in jury cases proposed voir dire and jury instructions. Unlisted witnesses (lay or expert) may testify only in extraordinary circumstances; unlisted exhibits need good cause. Motions in limine are due 28 days before trial and responses 7 days after filing. Stipulations of fact and (jury cases) a joint preliminary statement of no more than 1 page are due 10 days before trial. Unresolved objections to witnesses or exhibits are due 7 days before trial, with reasons and authority. Jury instructions: confer in person, then file one joint set s

docs.t: Judge Pamela Barker (N.D. Ohio) — Civil trial exhibits and logistics
docs.x: Judge Pamela Barker, N.D. Ohio. Civil trial exhibits and logistics: Trial runs 9 a.m. to about 4:30 p.m. in Room 16A; counsel appear at 8:30 a.m. Contact the courtroom deputy at 216-357-7240 at least 1 week before trial to visit the courtroom and test equipment. Each side’s exhibits go on a separate USB, CD, or DVD, received in Chambers 16A at least 2 business days before trial, using the naming convention -_.. All parties number their exhibits (“Plaintiff 1,” “Def 2”) with the case number on the sticker, exchange copies and indexes 2 business days before trial, and bring two binder sets with an index the morning of trial. Exhibits may be given to the jury during trial only with prior approval, and then with a copy for each juror. Continuance motions must state the reason and be endorsed by all moving parties and their lead counsel; conflict-based motions must attach the conflicting assi

docs.t: Judge Pamela Barker (N.D. Ohio) — Criminal cases (trap)
docs.x: Judge Pamela Barker, N.D. Ohio. Criminal cases (trap): Lead counsel and defendants must attend all proceedings unless excused on written motion; the final pretrial/change of plea is at 9 a.m. Notify the court in writing immediately of any discovery failure; a trial will not be continued for one. Pretrial motions, including suppression, are due 14 days before the final pretrial and oppositions 7 days before; any suppression hearing is held at the final pretrial, and the government must respond in writing to suppression motions. By 4 p.m. one week before trial, submit a trial brief containing a joint preliminary statement, signed stipulations, a joint set of jury instructions (agreed and disputed, with reasons and authority; agreed set also in Word on CD), proposed voir dire, evidentiary memoranda, and a length estimate. The court closely follows Sixth Circuit and FJC pattern instructions.

docs.t: Judge Patricia Anne Gaughan (N.D. Ohio) — Civil trial briefs (trap)
docs.x: Judge Patricia Anne Gaughan, N.D. Ohio. Civil trial briefs (trap): Trial briefs are required in every civil case, filed and exchanged at least 7 days before the final pretrial (or 7 days before trial if no final pretrial is set). They must include the facts, the controlling law with emphasis on issues that could support a full or partial Rule 50 motion, a witness list with testimony summaries, an exhibit index, likely evidentiary issues, and a trial-length estimate. Witnesses not listed in the trial brief may testify only in extraordinary circumstances (lay and expert alike); unlisted exhibits are excluded absent good cause. Motions in limine are filed with the trial brief; responses are due 3 days before the final pretrial. In jury cases the brief also carries proposed voir dire and jury instructions; in bench trials it incorporates numbered proposed findings (citing witnesses or exhibi

docs.t: Judge Patricia Anne Gaughan (N.D. Ohio) — Final pretrial
docs.x: Judge Patricia Anne Gaughan, N.D. Ohio. Final pretrial: Lead trial counsel and all parties must attend the final pretrial with full authority to discuss all aspects of the case, including pleadings, settlement, and scheduling.

docs.t: Judge Patricia Anne Gaughan (N.D. Ohio) — Jury instructions and voir dire
docs.x: Judge Patricia Anne Gaughan, N.D. Ohio. Jury instructions and voir dire: Counsel must confer in person on jury instructions and file one joint set: agreed instructions with authority, and disputed instructions with the proponent’s and objector’s reasons and authority. Instructions not submitted this way will not be considered, except ones that could not reasonably have been anticipated. Also provide the agreed instructions on a CD-ROM in Microsoft Word; alert security and avoid the x-ray machine when bringing it in. The court conducts initial voir dire; then one counsel per party may briefly question individual panel members on issues the court did not cover.

docs.t: Judge Patricia Anne Gaughan (N.D. Ohio) — Exhibits and depositions
docs.x: Judge Patricia Anne Gaughan, N.D. Ohio. Exhibits and depositions: Exchange all exhibits at least 2 working days before the trial date and give the court one copy on the day of trial; do not file exhibits. Plaintiff marks with numbers, defendant with letters (double letters, AA, BB, after 26), with the case number on each sticker; multiple parties prefix their last name (e.g., “Smith-1”), and joint exhibits are “Jt. Ex. 1.” Tabbed 3-ring binders with a table of contents are recommended. Give notice in the trial brief of depositions to be used at trial. Written objections are due at least 5 days before trial; the proponent then has 3 days to file a supporting brief or agree to delete the portion. Provide a complete written transcript of any videotaped deposition.

docs.t: Judge Patricia Anne Gaughan (N.D. Ohio) — Continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Patricia Anne Gaughan, N.D. Ohio. Continuances (trap): No trial or hearing is continued without a written motion stating the reason, endorsed in writing by all moving parties and their lead counsel. A motion based on a conflicting trial assignment will not be considered unless a copy of that assignment is attached.

docs.t: Judge Patricia Anne Gaughan (N.D. Ohio) — Case management conference
docs.x: Judge Patricia Anne Gaughan, N.D. Ohio. Case management conference: The CMC is by telephone, with the court placing the call. The parties hold their Rule 26(f) meeting beforehand, exchange initial disclosures within 10 days after it, and file the Report of Parties’ Planning Meeting (on the judge’s form) at least 3 work days before the CMC. Plaintiff’s counsel must confirm that defense counsel (or an unrepresented defendant) received the CMC notice. Disclosures and discovery are not filed except to support a motion or for trial. Questions go to (216) 357-7210. Patent cases follow the Local Patent Rules: the planning report must propose dates through claim construction (with reasons for any departure), anticipated motions and early summary judgment issues, the nature of the dispute, any need for extra interrogatories or depositions, the protective order (Appendix C form or an alternative),

docs.t: Judge Patricia Anne Gaughan (N.D. Ohio) — Criminal pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Patricia Anne Gaughan, N.D. Ohio. Criminal pretrial (trap): Counsel must notify the court in writing immediately of any failure to provide discovery; the court will not continue a trial over a discovery failure if this was not done. Pretrial motions, including suppression motions, must state a substantial foundation explicitly. Any suppression hearing is held on the final pretrial date. By 4:00 p.m. 2 working days before the final pretrial, submit a trial brief with stipulations signed by all counsel and the defendant, a joint set of jury instructions (agreed and disputed, as in civil cases, plus a CD-ROM), proposed voir dire, memoranda on anticipated evidentiary and legal issues, and a trial-length estimate. The court follows Sixth Circuit and Federal Judicial Center pattern instructions as closely as possible. Exhibits are marked as in civil cases.

docs.t: Judge Solomon Oliver Jr. (N.D. Ohio) — Case management conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Solomon Oliver Jr., N.D. Ohio. Case management conference (trap): Local Rule 16.3(b) attendance is enforced: both parties and lead counsel must attend. For an entity, the party is the person most familiar with the facts, not in-house counsel or someone who merely has settlement authority. A motion to excuse attendance for undue hardship must be filed well in advance. Plaintiff’s counsel arranges the Rule 26(f) meeting and must confirm that defendants received the CMC order. The jointly signed planning report, substantially in the court’s form, is due at least 3 days before the CMC. No formal discovery before the CMC except as needed for jurisdictional challenges or emergency, temporary, or preliminary relief (LR 26.2); Rule 26(a) disclosures are unaffected. If the case resolves first, submit a jointly signed stipulation or notify the court.

docs.t: Judge Solomon Oliver Jr. (N.D. Ohio) — Final pretrial conference
docs.x: Judge Solomon Oliver Jr., N.D. Ohio. Final pretrial conference: Parties and lead counsel must attend with full authority to discuss all aspects of the case, including settlement. Counsel must confer with clients and each other on settlement posture at least 2 business days before the conference.

docs.t: Judge Solomon Oliver Jr. (N.D. Ohio) — Civil pretrial deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Solomon Oliver Jr., N.D. Ohio. Civil pretrial deadlines (trap): Daubert/Kumho motions are due 10 days after all dispositive motions are resolved, with responses 7 days and replies 5 days after that. Other motions in limine are due 14 days before trial, responses 7 days later. 7 days before trial: trial briefs (facts, full citations, evidentiary issues), witness and exhibit lists with descriptions and purpose, proposed voir dire questions, exchange of proposed jury instructions and interrogatories, and in bench trials numbered proposed findings and conclusions citing witnesses or exhibits. 3 days before trial: exchange of exhibits, stipulations of fact, a joint preliminary statement of the case (1 page maximum, delivered to chambers), unresolved objections to witnesses and exhibits with authority, and a single joint jury-instruction filing divided into agreed, plaintiff’s disputed,

docs.t: Judge Solomon Oliver Jr. (N.D. Ohio) — Depositions at trial
docs.x: Judge Solomon Oliver Jr., N.D. Ohio. Depositions at trial: Give opposing counsel transcript designations 14 days before trial; cross-designations are due 7 days before. File unresolved objections 3 days before trial, attaching and highlighting the objected-to portions with objections noted in the margin. A complete transcript of any video deposition must be filed before it is used.

docs.t: Judge Solomon Oliver Jr. (N.D. Ohio) — Exhibits
docs.x: Judge Solomon Oliver Jr., N.D. Ohio. Exhibits: Mark exhibits “Jt. Ex. 1,” “Pl. Ex. 1,” and “Deft. Ex. A” (third parties by surname and letter; party surnames added in multiparty cases; double letters after 26), and number each page of multipage exhibits (Pl. Ex. 1-1). File duplicates as joint exhibits. Deliver the court’s copy directly to chambers, not the Clerk; counsel keep the originals for trial.

docs.t: Judge Solomon Oliver Jr. (N.D. Ohio) — Trial days
docs.x: Judge Solomon Oliver Jr., N.D. Ohio. Trial days: Trial runs 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. with a one-hour lunch and 15-minute morning and afternoon breaks. Raise issues needing attention outside the jury’s presence with staff; expect them to be handled before or after the trial day or at breaks. Parties must be present whenever the jury is seated unless excused. By 4:00 p.m. the day before trial and by the close of each trial day, give opposing counsel the next day’s witnesses in order. Have enough witnesses to fill each trial day. The court conducts voir dire with limited follow-up by counsel. Objection grounds to jury instructions are taken up at a charge conference before closing statements.

docs.t: Judge Solomon Oliver Jr. (N.D. Ohio) — Continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Solomon Oliver Jr., N.D. Ohio. Continuances (trap): A civil trial continuance needs a written motion stating the reason, endorsed by all moving parties and their lead counsel, showing all other counsel’s consent or certifying efforts to obtain it. A motion based on a conflicting trial assignment must attach a copy of that assignment and be filed within 2 days after counsel learns of the conflict. The criminal order requires a written motion with the conflicting assignment attached, filed (as written) “not less that fifteen (15) days after” counsel learns of the conflict and at least 30 days before trial.

docs.t: Judge Solomon Oliver Jr. (N.D. Ohio) — Criminal cases
docs.x: Judge Solomon Oliver Jr., N.D. Ohio. Criminal cases: Counsel appear at least 30 minutes before trial time. No plea agreement is accepted later than 1 week before trial. On the discovery deadline, notify the court in writing of any failure to provide discovery; each pretrial motion must state its foundation (Local Rule 12.1). By 4:00 p.m. on the set date, submit a jointly prepared neutral statement of the case, stipulations signed by counsel and defendant, voir dire questions and jury instructions (disputed ones with authority), and evidentiary memoranda. Exchange demonstratives 2 days before trial and submit two copies of all exhibits in a binder with an index by the morning of trial; exhibits go to the jury only with approval and enough copies for every juror.

docs.t: Judge A. Joe Fish (N.D. Tex.) — Case management and scheduling
docs.x: Judge A. Joe Fish, N.D. Tex.. Case management and scheduling: No Rule 16 preliminary pretrial conference and no Rule 26(f) conference. After an answer is filed, the judge issues a status report order requiring a joint status report, then a scheduling order that sets deadlines and specifically modifies some Local Rules. Initial Rule 26(a)(1) disclosures are due within thirty days of the status report order, with notice of the disclosures filed with the clerk. Discovery matters are routinely referred to a magistrate judge.

docs.t: Judge A. Joe Fish (N.D. Tex.) — Proposed orders (trap)
docs.x: Judge A. Joe Fish, N.D. Tex.. Proposed orders (trap): A proposed order is required with EVERY motion. Email it in Word or WordPerfect to Fish_Orders@txnd.uscourts.gov, with the case number and the motion’s document number in the subject line, copying opposing counsel.

docs.t: Judge A. Joe Fish (N.D. Tex.) — Filing format (trap)
docs.x: Judge A. Joe Fish, N.D. Tex.. Filing format (trap): Never combine an answer and a motion (including a motion to dismiss) in one pleading, or a response and a motion in one document. Every document must carry the full case number, ending with the judge’s letter designation “G.” Faxed documents, including faxed attachments or exhibits, are not accepted.

docs.t: Judge A. Joe Fish (N.D. Tex.) — Motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge A. Joe Fish, N.D. Tex.. Motions (trap): Dispositive motions typically must be filed at least 100 days before the trial date; the scheduling order sets the summary judgment deadline. Oral argument is rarely granted. Any request to change a trial date must be made in writing before the discovery deadline. Motions in limine must be confined to matters actually in dispute and are due by the scheduling-order deadline; no brief is required.

docs.t: Judge A. Joe Fish (N.D. Tex.) — Settlement meeting (trap)
docs.x: Judge A. Joe Fish, N.D. Tex.. Settlement meeting (trap): Parties and lead counsel must meet face to face to discuss settlement at least 10 days before the final pretrial conference, and jointly file a written report within 7 days after the meeting stating whether meaningful progress was made and the prospects of settlement.

docs.t: Judge A. Joe Fish (N.D. Tex.) — Pretrial disclosures and pretrial order
docs.x: Judge A. Joe Fish, N.D. Tex.. Pretrial disclosures and pretrial order: Witness lists under L.R. 26.2 must classify each witness as probable, possible, expert, or record custodian, with name, address, and a brief narrative summary of expected testimony. Exhibit lists must come with a written statement signed by counsel for each non-offering party stating, per exhibit, whether admissibility is agreed and the nature and legal basis of any objection, and who urges it. Beyond L.R. 16.4, the pretrial order must state the estimated length of trial and whether the case is jury or non-jury.

docs.t: Judge A. Joe Fish (N.D. Tex.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge A. Joe Fish, N.D. Tex.. Trial: The judge conducts voir dire; counsel may submit written questions in advance, and the judge typically asks afterward whether other issues should be addressed. Requested jury instructions and proposed findings and conclusions must be annotated. Parties may use their own exhibit stickers. Courtroom decorum is governed by the Order Regarding Conduct of Trial issued before or at the pretrial conference. For electronic equipment, call chambers at 214-753-2310.

docs.t: Judge A. Joe Fish (N.D. Tex.) — Chambers copies and contact
docs.x: Judge A. Joe Fish, N.D. Tex.. Chambers copies and contact: Since March 23, 2020, the judge’s-copy requirement for electronically filed documents is suspended; no judge’s copy is required. All calls go through chambers at 214-753-2310, including procedural questions not answered by the rules, scheduling questions, and the status of a motion or proposed order. Another party may sign on an attorney’s behalf if that attorney agrees.

docs.t: Judge Brantley Starr (N.D. Tex.) — Extensions of time (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brantley Starr, N.D. Tex.. Extensions of time (trap): Any motion or stipulation to extend a deadline must be filed at least 2 days before the deadline (at least 5 days in a sealed case, to give the Clerk’s office time to deliver it to chambers). Absent extraordinary circumstances, requests filed 2 days or less before the deadline will not be considered, and the underlying motion will be deemed unopposed.

docs.t: Judge Brantley Starr (N.D. Tex.) — Proposed orders and judge’s copies
docs.x: Judge Brantley Starr, N.D. Tex.. Proposed orders and judge’s copies: Every motion requires a proposed order emailed in Word (not PDF) to Starr_Orders@txnd.uscourts.gov, with the case number and the motion’s document number in the subject line. Since 3/24/2020 the judge has suspended the judge’s-copy requirement; no paper copy of e-filed documents is required.

docs.t: Judge Brantley Starr (N.D. Tex.) — Conduct and in-person appearance (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brantley Starr, N.D. Tex.. Conduct and in-person appearance (trap): By litigating before Judge Starr, counsel and pro se parties represent that they have read and will follow Dondi Properties Corp. v. Commerce Savings & Loan Ass’n, 121 F.R.D. 284 (N.D. Tex. 1988), the Local Civil or Criminal Rules, the Texas Lawyer’s Creed, and the Texas Rules of Professional Conduct. Every attorney admitted in the district or pro hac vice represents being willing and able to appear in person whenever ordered; the court aims to give at least 7 days’ notice of in-person hearings. Failing to appear in person can bring sanctions, including revocation of pro hac vice status, and a request to continue a setting must explain in detail why counsel cannot appear in person. No separate AI certificate is required; follow Local Civil Rule 7.2(f) and Local Criminal Rule 47.2(e) on disclosing generative-AI use.

docs.t: Judge Brantley Starr (N.D. Tex.) — Scheduling proposal
docs.x: Judge Brantley Starr, N.D. Tex.. Scheduling proposal: The posted Meet and Confer Template is a Joint Proposal for Contents of Scheduling and Discovery Order: proposed discovery, trial (days, jury or bench), motion, joinder, amendment, expert, and settlement-negotiation deadlines, plus a settlement status report (no settlement figures in a non-jury case), views on mediation, consent to a magistrate judge, and a discovery plan and limits. The template notes the court encourages early mediation or arbitration.

docs.t: Judge Brantley Starr (N.D. Tex.) — Criminal sentencing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brantley Starr, N.D. Tex.. Criminal sentencing (trap): A filing made less than 7 days before sentencing lets the court unilaterally reset the sentencing to a later week. Do not read the sentencing memo or character letters aloud; the court has already read them. Each side gets up to 30 minutes for 3553(a) and variance argument plus victim or character witnesses (not counting allocution or argument and witnesses on objections). If you need more, move at least 1 week before sentencing; the court may stop you if you exceed the time. A revocation will not proceed unless all counsel email the courtroom deputy the parties’ agreement on which allegations the defendant pleads true and not true.

docs.t: Judge Brantley Starr (N.D. Tex.) — Criminal detention
docs.x: Judge Brantley Starr, N.D. Tex.. Criminal detention: Review of a magistrate judge’s detention ruling is a legal review only, with argument but no new evidence. To offer new evidence, brief why it was unavailable earlier or other good cause; the court typically remands to the magistrate judge if the showing is made. A defendant on pretrial release is taken into custody on a guilty verdict. A motion for release is referred to the duty magistrate judge for expedited consideration, often not on the verdict day.

docs.t: Judge Brantley Starr (N.D. Tex.) — Pretrial filings and voir dire
docs.x: Judge Brantley Starr, N.D. Tex.. Pretrial filings and voir dire: Submit deposition designations only for witnesses unavailable under Rule 32. The scheduling order requires a joint filing with all designations, an FRE rule number for each page/line objection, written explanations of objections and responses (in place of sidebars), and the full depositions. The court asks a first round of voir dire, then allows counsel 15–30 minutes per side. Proposed voir dire must be questions counsel will ask; questions not preapproved at the pretrial conference are not allowed (other than reasonable follow-up). Settle at least two weeks before trial. A settlement during trial moots the case and discharges the jury only if its terms are filed unredacted or disclosed in open court; confidentiality is available only before the jury is sworn.

docs.t: Judge Brantley Starr (N.D. Tex.) — Exhibits and demonstratives at trial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brantley Starr, N.D. Tex.. Exhibits and demonstratives at trial (trap): By 6 p.m. each evening, email opposing counsel and court staff the next day’s witnesses and exhibits (exhibits in numerical order). By 8 p.m., opposing counsel responds with the written objections it maintains, in explanatory rather than shorthand form; argument is heard in a session starting about 8:30 a.m., before the jury arrives at 8:45 a.m. Overruling objections does not admit an exhibit; exhibits are admitted only in front of the jury with a witness on the stand. Foundation and authenticity rulings are reserved until trial unless a compliant FRE 803(6)/902(11) affidavit is used; a provider’s affidavit for emails covers only headers, and each email’s content must meet Rule 803(6)’s five requirements. Opening and closing demonstratives must be exchanged by email, copying court personnel, by 6 p.m. the night

docs.t: Judge Brantley Starr (N.D. Tex.) — Trial conduct and time limits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brantley Starr, N.D. Tex.. Trial conduct and time limits (trap): Cross may not exceed the scope of direct (recross, redirect) unless the parties agree. If both sides list a witness, confer before the pretrial conference about calling the witness once with wide-open cross. Objections during opening or closing are highly disfavored; the court holds a sidebar afterward for curative-instruction or new-trial requests, but will interrupt and admonish counsel before the jury for a limine violation. No speaking objections: state the rule number (“Objection. 611.”) or one or two words, or ask for a sidebar. Civil trials and some criminal trials have per-party hour limits set at the pretrial conference or by order. Time before the jury and lost sidebars count (drawn sidebars are split); requests for more time must state how much and proffer what it will yield, and inefficient use weighs agai

docs.t: Judge Brian McKay (N.D. Tex.) — Conference before motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brian McKay, N.D. Tex.. Conference before motions (trap): Before any non-dispositive motion, the movant must meaningfully confer with every affected party to learn whether the motion is opposed, and include a L.R. 7.1(b) certificate of conference. Not required for motions to dismiss, for judgment on the pleadings, or for summary judgment, or when a conference is not possible (the certificate must then explain why). Motions filed after a superficial attempt, or no attempt, to confer are subject to denial.

docs.t: Judge Brian McKay (N.D. Tex.) — Motion practice
docs.x: Judge Brian McKay, N.D. Tex.. Motion practice: The Local Rules’ default deadlines and page limits apply unless ordered otherwise. The judge strictly enforces L.R. 7.1(i) and 56.6 on supporting materials, and briefs must cite supporting materials by appendix page number (L.R. 7.2(e), 56.5(c)).

docs.t: Judge Brian McKay (N.D. Tex.) — Oral argument
docs.x: Judge Brian McKay, N.D. Tex.. Oral argument: The judge generally rules on the briefs but may hold argument sua sponte or on request. A request that represents a junior lawyer will primarily handle the hearing weighs in favor of holding one, though it does not guarantee a hearing.

docs.t: Judge Brian McKay (N.D. Tex.) — Proposed orders and courtesy copies
docs.x: Judge Brian McKay, N.D. Tex.. Proposed orders and courtesy copies: Submit proposed orders through ECF. For an agreed proposed order, also email a Word version to mckay_orders@txnd.uscourts.gov. No paper copies of electronically filed documents are required.

docs.t: Judge Brian McKay (N.D. Tex.) — Filing and ECF (trap)
docs.x: Judge Brian McKay, N.D. Tex.. Filing and ECF (trap): Under L.R. 5.1(e), the judge allows paper filing; e-filing is permitted but not required. Even so, all attorneys and unrepresented parties (except pro se prisoners) must register as ECF users and consent to electronic service unless excused for good cause.

docs.t: Judge Brian McKay (N.D. Tex.) — Local counsel and sealing
docs.x: Judge Brian McKay, N.D. Tex.. Local counsel and sealing: L.R. 83.10(a) is strictly enforced; to proceed without local counsel, file a motion showing good cause. Do not unreasonably file under seal: file unsealed as much as you reasonably can consistent with any protective order. Redact Social Security and taxpayer-ID numbers, financial-account numbers, minors’ names, and dates of birth.

docs.t: Judge Brian McKay (N.D. Tex.) — Consent to magistrate judge
docs.x: Judge Brian McKay, N.D. Tex.. Consent to magistrate judge: Parties may consent under 28 U.S.C. § 636(c) through the ECF electronic-consent option or the court’s Notice and Election form; consent is voluntary and may be withheld without adverse substantive consequences.

docs.t: Judge Brian McKay (N.D. Tex.) — Contacting chambers
docs.x: Judge Brian McKay, N.D. Tex.. Contacting chambers: Contact with chambers other than through filings is strongly discouraged; do not ask staff questions answered by the rules or orders. Case information is available from the ECF Help Desk at (214) 753-2633. Call the courtroom deputy, Angelica Aguilar, at (214) 753-2183 only to alert the court to a matter genuinely needing urgent attention.

docs.t: Judge David C. Godbey (N.D. Tex.) — Professional conduct (trap)

docs.x: Judge David C. Godbey, N.D. Tex.. docs.t: Judge David C. Godbey (N.D. Tex.) — Standard protective order: designations and challenges
docs.x: Judge David C. Godbey, N.D. Tex.. Standard protective order: designations and challenges: Two tiers: “Confidential Information” and “Confidential Attorney Eyes Only.” Deposition testimony may be designated at the deposition or in writing within 14 calendar days, and is treated as Attorney Eyes Only during that period. To challenge a designation, ask in writing; the producing party has 10 business days to respond, and after that and the LR 7.1(a) conference the receiving party may move. The designation stands until the court rules. Confidential material may go to 2 identified employees, 2 in-house counsel, outside counsel, staff, experts, and vendors; Attorney Eyes Only excludes employees and in-house counsel.

docs.t: Judge David C. Godbey (N.D. Tex.) — Standard protective order: experts, filing, and return
docs.x: Judge David C. Godbey, N.D. Tex.. Standard protective order: experts, filing, and return: Before disclosure to an expert, consultant, or employee, serve a signed Exhibit A agreement, CV, affiliation, and consulting history; the producing party has 10 business days to object in writing for good cause, and nothing may be disclosed in the meantime. Confidential information submitted to the court must be filed under seal. Within 60 calendar days after final judgment (including appeals) or settlement dismissal, return or destroy designated material and certify it; outside counsel may keep court papers and work product.

docs.t: Judge David C. Godbey (N.D. Tex.) — Chambers and contact
docs.x: Judge David C. Godbey, N.D. Tex.. Chambers and contact: Dallas, Courtroom 1505; case letter designation (N). Judicial assistant Donna Hocker Beyer (214-753-2700); courtroom deputy Carla Moore (214-753-2706).

docs.x: Judge Ed Kinkeade, N.D. Tex.. docs.x: Judge Ed Kinkeade, N.D. Tex.. Scheduling and settlement: No Rule 16 preliminary pretrial conference. Rule 26(f) conferences may be in person or by phone. The joint status report must discuss settlement status and prospects, with more than a statement that talks failed. Where the judge requires local counsel, local counsel must sign all filings under Rule 11 and comply with L.R. 83.10(b).

The court prefers a dispositive-motion deadline at least 120 days before trial (never fewer than 90) and after the discovery deadline, and a trial date within 18 months of the complaint absent exceptional circumstances. docs.x: Judge James Wesley Hendrix, N.D. Tex.. docs.t: Judge Kasdin Mitchell (N.D. Tex.) — Joint scheduling proposal: other contents
docs.x: Judge Kasdin Mitchell, N.D. Tex.. State whether the parties consent to trial (jury or non-jury) before a magistrate judge, any other relevant matters, and whether the parties want a conference with the court, and why.

docs.t: Judge Kasdin Mitchell (N.D. Tex.) — Contact
docs.x: Judge Kasdin Mitchell, N.D. Tex.. Contact: Chambers: 214-753-2420. Courtroom deputy: Shakira Todd, 214-753-2421. Dallas, 1100 Commerce Street, Room 1376E; case letter (M).

Required for: proposed amended scheduling orders; proposed protective orders (no separate order granting the motion needed); and non-dispositive motions in all prisoner § 1983 and habeas cases, consent or not. docs.t: Judge Lee Ann Reno (N.D. Tex.) — Emergency or expedited motions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Lee Ann Reno, N.D. Tex..
